styles.features: tiny dense dots of pure colour; Zeeland beaches, dunes, fishermen and women in local costume and caps; restrained sea-green, ochre and blue; quiet horizontal compositions with low horizons
styles.note: Describe the dotted coastal work, not his later linear Symbolist drawings.

styles.name: Henry van de Velde (painting)
styles.features: pointillist dots stretching into rhythmic dashes; Flemish peasants in fields, beaches and gardens; strokes following the contours of forms in flowing curves; restrained earthy tones with blue and yellow light

styles.name: Willy Finch
styles.features: precise even pointillist dots; Belgian and English coastlines, harbour piers, chalk cliffs, horse racing on sand; calm horizons; pale silvery blues, sand yellows and soft greens; clear restrained light

styles.name: Giuseppe Pellizza da Volpedo
styles.features: fine dots and short divided strokes; sunlit Piedmont countryside; solemn peasants and labourers advancing in frieze-like rows; warm golden-ochre light and luminous haze; symmetrical monumental staging

styles.name: Angelo Morbelli
styles.features: fine interlaced filaments of colour; silvery grey and pale violet light; rows of women weeding flooded rice fields; elderly men seated in long hospice halls under tall windows; melancholy stillness

styles.name: Gaetano Previati
styles.features: long flowing threadlike strokes like streams of light; ethereal elongated figures, Madonnas, angels and mothers; diffuse golden and pale blue glow; dematerialised blurred forms; vertical rising rhythms

styles.name: Henri Martin
styles.medium: oil on canvas, large decorative panels
styles.features: broad stippled dabs of colour; Occitan stone villages, terraced gardens, pergolas, haymakers and contemplative figures; muted golden green, violet and ochre; misty diffused sunlight; calm mural-scale compositions
styles.note: The French painter born 1860, Toulouse.

styles.name: Henri Le Sidaner
styles.features: soft vibrating dabs of paint; deserted laid tables in gardens, rose arbours, village houses with glowing windows at dusk; mauve, blue and gold twilight; no figures, quiet suggested presence

styles.name: Émile Bernard
styles.features: Cloisonnism: flat areas of bright colour enclosed by strong dark outlines like enamel; Breton women in white coifs, meadows, religious pardons; no modelling, high horizon; yellow, red, green planes

styles.name: Louis Anquetin
styles.features: Cloisonnist dark outlines and flat colour; whole scenes bathed in one dominant hue, deep blue dusk or golden yellow noon; Parisian boulevards, lit shopfronts, horse cabs, reapers; poster-like simplicity

styles.name: Paul Sérusier
styles.features: simplified flat patches of pure colour, near-abstract landscapes; Breton women, beech woods, harvests; saturated orange, olive and violet; rhythmic decorative contours; tapestry-like flattened surface

styles.name: Charles Filiger
styles.features: small precise gouaches in flat clear colour; hieratic saints and Madonnas with halos, simplified Breton landscapes; geometric mosaic-like borders and symmetrical patterns; Byzantine and early Italian stiffness; jewel tones

styles.name: Meijer de Haan
styles.features: flat dark-outlined forms; still lifes of onions, jugs and fruit; Breton farm interiors with women spinning hemp; heavy contours, simplified volumes; deep earthy browns with red and green accents

styles.name: Charles Laval
styles.features: synthetist tropical landscapes; lush Caribbean vegetation, women by streams, slopes and sea; flattened planes with firm outlines; warm greens, ochres and pinks; decorative rhythmic foliage and parallel brush hatching

styles.name: Henry Moret
styles.features: vigorous broken strokes of bright colour; rugged Breton coast, granite cliffs, coves, seaweed gatherers; synthetist simplified masses; emerald sea, orange rocks, violet shadows; clear Atlantic light

styles.name: Maxime Maufra
styles.features: energetic brushwork with bold synthetist contours; Breton harbours, fishing boats, granite cliffs and stormy seas; strong blues against rust and gold; simplified massive rocks and rolling waves

styles.name: Roderic O'Conor
styles.features: vivid parallel stripes of unmixed colour laid like ribbons; Breton cliffs, wheatfields, peasant girls; strong reds, oranges, greens and purples; energetic directional rhythm; flattened intense space

styles.name: Armand Seguin
styles.medium: etching and colour zincography on paper
styles.features: sinuous decorative printed lines; Breton hills, fishing villages, women in coifs; bold black outlines and flat tones; curving rhythmic trees and fields; sparse soft colour over strong linear design

styles.name: Władysław Ślewiński
styles.features: subdued synthetist painting; rocky Breton coasts, still lifes of fish and fruit, sober portraits; flattened forms with firm contours; restrained greys, ochres and cool blues; quiet calm mood

styles.name: Cuno Amiet
styles.features: intense flat colour from Pont-Aven synthetism; Swiss orchards, apple harvests, snowy fields and gardens; bright contrasting orange, blue and green; simplified bold forms; dense rhythmic dabs

styles.name: Pierre Bonnard
styles.features: shimmering mottled patches of saturated colour; intimate interiors, bathtubs, sunlit breakfast tables, gardens seen from windows; figures dissolving into patterned surroundings; violet, orange, yellow; high viewpoints and cropped edges

styles.name: Édouard Vuillard
styles.features: matte chalky paint on cardboard; intimate rooms where figures merge into patterned wallpaper, fabrics and carpets; muted browns, ochres, plum and sage; flattened space packed with small decorative motifs

styles.name: Maurice Denis
styles.features: flat decorative surfaces with soft rounded contours; pale pink, mauve and mint green; women in white dresses, mothers with children, processions in gardens; rhythmic arabesques; serene frieze-like groups

styles.name: Félix Vallotton
styles.features: stark woodcut with large solid black masses and minimal line; crowds, street incidents and bourgeois interiors in silhouette; strong graphic contrast; flat shapes without gradation; cool ironic economy

styles.name: Ker-Xavier Roussel
styles.features: soft feathery brushwork; mythological pastorals with nymphs, fauns and bacchic dances in luminous groves; tender greens, rose and golden light; dreamy tapestry-like decorative composition

styles.name: Paul Ranson
styles.medium: oil and distemper on canvas, tapestry design
styles.features: flat decorative arabesques anticipating Art Nouveau; esoteric scenes of witches, nudes and stylised plants; sinuous curving outlines; flat ochre, green and orange; ornamental patterning like tapestry

styles.name: József Rippl-Rónai
styles.features: short thick dabs of colour like grains of corn; cosy Hungarian interiors, family members, gardens; warm saturated reds, yellows and greens; flat decorative arrangement; patterned cloths and furniture

styles.name: Georges Lacombe
styles.features: Breton seascapes with waves and rocks turned into flowing arabesques; flat saturated colour, vermilion and ochre cliffs, emerald sea; stylised trees; Japanese-print simplification and decorative rhythm

styles.name: Jan Verkade
styles.features: simplified flat Breton landscapes and still lifes with solid outlines; muted earthy greens and ochres; later hieratic religious murals with geometric proportions, frontal figures and calm symmetry

styles.name: Suzanne Valadon
styles.features: thick dark contours around robust bodies; bold flat colour in strong reds, blues and greens; nudes, women bathing, patterned fabrics and flower bouquets; frank unidealised figures; dense compact composition

styles.name: Harold Gilman
styles.features: thick dabs of paint laid like a mosaic; modest London interiors, lodging-house rooms, women at tables, washstands; bright patches of strong colour; flat simplified forms; carefully ordered frontal composition

styles.name: Jens Ferdinand Willumsen
styles.medium: oil on canvas, enamel and relief
styles.features: synthetist flat colour with bold contours; Breton women and towering Nordic mountain landscapes; later harsh luminous hues, clashing yellow and blue; stylised dramatic forms and decorative inlaid frames

styles.name: Viktor Borisov-Musatov
styles.features: faded tapestry-like tones of grey-blue, green and lilac; dreamy women in crinoline dresses in old manor parks, by ponds and colonnades; flattened space; soft dry matte texture; melancholy stillness

styles.name: Ivan Aguéli
styles.medium: oil on small canvas and panel
styles.features: small panels with simplified flat colour planes; quiet Gotland landscapes, Paris outskirts, Egyptian desert with white cubic houses; soft luminous pastel tones; geometric calm and very few details

styles.name: Pekka Halonen
styles.features: synthetist simplification of the Finnish winter; snow-laden pines, frozen lakes, washerwomen on ice; broad flat areas of white with blue shadow; dark silhouettes and decorative contours; Japanese-print composition

styles.name: Dante Gabriel Rossetti
styles.features: Half-length women filling the frame, heavy-lidded eyes, full red lips, masses of crimped auburn hair and long necks; jewel-toned greens and crimsons; flat shallow space crowded with flowers, fabrics and decorative objects.

styles.name: John Everett Millais, Pre-Raphaelite period
styles.medium: oil on wet white ground, canvas
styles.features: Hard-edged foliage and flowers painted leaf by leaf over a bright white ground; saturated clear greens; even daylight with few shadows; figures in medieval or contemporary dress with stiff, intense poses.

styles.name: William Holman Hunt
styles.features: Intense saturated colour with violet shadows, acid greens and oranges; every surface rendered in close detail; glaring sunlight or lamplight; many symbolic objects; figures with strained, earnest expressions.

styles.name: Ford Madox Brown
styles.features: Crowded compositions with figures pressed close to the picture plane, sharp outdoor light, hard local colour, realistic unflattering faces, careful period costume and street detail, sometimes in circular or arched formats.

styles.name: Arthur Hughes
styles.features: Luminous violet and emerald harmonies; twilight and moonlit gardens; ivy, ferns and blossom in minute detail; slender young lovers or maidens in medieval dress; soft, melancholy evening light.

styles.name: Edward Burne-Jones
styles.medium: oil, gouache and watercolour; tapestry designs
styles.features: Elongated pale androgynous figures with dreamy downcast faces, heavy pleated drapery and polished armour; muted greys, stone, dusky rose and bronze; shallow frieze-like space with briar roses and rocky Renaissance-style landscapes.

styles.name: John William Waterhouse
styles.features: Young women with long auburn or chestnut hair in flowing medieval or classical gowns; reeds, lilies and dark pond water; loose but solid academic brushwork; soft diffused light, moss greens, deep blues and warm skin tones.

styles.name: Evelyn De Morgan
styles.medium: oil on canvas with gold highlights
styles.features: Allegorical figures in billowing translucent drapery with crisp flame-like folds, gold highlights, clear Botticelli-like contours, rainbow and sunrise glows against dark grounds, symmetrical groupings of angels, spirits and personified virtues.

styles.name: Marie Spartali Stillman
styles.features: Soft opaque watercolour; Italianate gardens and Florentine settings; women in rich brocaded Renaissance dress; muted rose, gold and sage harmonies; quiet literary scenes framed by lush flowers.

styles.name: Eleanor Fortescue-Brickdale
styles.features: Bright clear watercolour with crisp outlines; jewel-like medieval costumes in vermilion, gold and blue; flowering meadows and castle backgrounds; detailed heraldic and floral patterning; storybook clarity of narrative.

styles.name: George Frederic Watts
styles.features: Hazy, scumbled, dry paint surface; monumental sculptural allegorical figures merging into misty blue-green and golden atmospheres; vague cosmic spaces; dim glowing light and softened contours.

styles.name: Frederic Leighton
styles.features: Polished academic finish; idealised classical figures with marble-smooth skin; glowing translucent drapery in saturated orange, saffron and rose; sunlit Mediterranean seas and terraces; sinuous relaxed poses.

styles.name: Albert Moore
styles.features: Classical women in clinging pale drapery arranged in frieze-like rows; flat decorative backgrounds of flowers, fans and patterned textiles; delicate harmonies of apricot, cream, primrose and pale green; no narrative action.

styles.name: James McNeill Whistler
styles.medium: oil on canvas, thin liquid glazes
styles.features: Thin, liquid, nearly transparent veils of paint; near-monochrome harmonies of blue-grey, silver or black; river at night with blurred lights; sparse Japanese-influenced composition; figures as flat dark silhouettes.

styles.name: Aubrey Beardsley
styles.medium: pen and black ink on paper
styles.features: Stark black-and-white pen drawing: large flat black masses against white, hairline contours, dense stippled and peacock-feather ornament, elongated elegant or grotesque figures, asymmetric Japanese-style layout, no tonal shading.
styles.note: Keep strictly monochrome; avoid the explicit content of some originals

styles.name: Margaret Macdonald Mackintosh
styles.medium: painted gesso panels with twine, beads and inlaid glass
styles.features: Low-relief gesso with raised outlines of string and inset beads and coloured glass; tall attenuated stylised female figures enclosed by rose motifs and long vertical lines; muted pinks, silver, mauve and pale green.

styles.name: Phoebe Anna Traquair
styles.features: Dense glowing surfaces of gold, crimson and blue; angels with multicoloured wings; crowded celestial hosts; Celtic interlace and medieval illumination borders; small jewel-like figures in flat decorative space.

styles.name: John Duncan, Scottish Celtic Revival
styles.features: Smooth tempera with clear outlines and flat bright colour; figures from Celtic legend in embroidered robes; interlace borders; sea-girt islands and blue Highland seas; riders and angels processing in a frieze.

styles.name: Harry Clarke
styles.medium: stained glass; ink and watercolour book illustration
styles.features: Intensely saturated deep blues and rubies; glass divided by dense black leading and fine etched detail; elongated pallid figures with large eyes and long fingers; jewel-encrusted robes; intricate ornament filling every space.

styles.name: Gustave Moreau
styles.features: Jewel-like glazed colour over dark grounds; fine gold and black line drawing floating over the paint; encrusted ornament and gems; hieratic mythological figures in exotic architecture; some passages left as thick knife-laid paint.

styles.name: Pierre Puvis de Chavannes
styles.features: Pale chalky fresco-like surfaces in muted grey, lilac, pale ochre and blue-green; flattened frieze compositions of calm static classical figures in simple landscapes; minimal modelling, horizontal calm, no strong shadows.

styles.name: Eugène Carrière
styles.features: Near-monochrome brown and umber haze; figures emerging from smoky darkness with soft blurred contours; only faces and hands lit; intimate mother-and-child groups and portraits fading to nothing at the edges.

styles.name: Lucien Lévy-Dhurmer
styles.features: Soft pastel in cool blues, aquamarine and violet; mysterious women with closed eyes or mask-like faces; misted Mediterranean coasts and Venetian or Breton twilights; delicate gradations of light.

styles.name: Carlos Schwabe
styles.features: Precise thin outlines with pale watercolour washes; mystical maidens, angels and figures of Death; lilies, irises and thorny vines wrapping the composition; cool green, ivory and lavender; Gothic linear elegance.

styles.name: Maurice Denis, Nabis
styles.features: Flat decorative areas of soft pink, mauve and pale green with dotted, stippled textures; simplified rounded figures; sinuous arabesque contours; devotional and family scenes in gardens; tapestry-like surface.

styles.name: Paul Gauguin, Synthetism
styles.features: Flat areas of unmodulated saturated orange, magenta, ochre and deep green bordered by dark outlines; coarse visible canvas weave; simplified monumental figures; non-naturalistic red or pink ground; decorative tropical plants.

styles.name: Fernand Khnopff
styles.features: Cool frozen stillness; pale smooth surfaces; androgynous women with fixed stares; blues and greys touched with gold; empty canals of a silent old town; precise drawing and hermetic symbolic objects.

styles.name: Jean Delville
styles.features: Swirling luminous cosmic compositions; idealised figures dissolving into flame-like rays; intense blue, gold and violet; precise academic drawing combined with mystical radiance and serpentine rhythmic lines.

styles.name: William Degouve de Nuncques
styles.features: Nocturnal scenes in deep blue; a single lit house or window under dark sky; black silhouetted trees; still mirror-like water; empty parks; flat calm surfaces and uncanny silence without figures.

styles.name: Léon Spilliaert
styles.medium: ink wash, gouache and pastel on paper
styles.features: Dark ink washes on paper; empty seafronts, dykes and promenades receding in steep diagonal perspective; lonely black-clad figures; flat inky blacks with glints of light; muted grey-blue and ochre.

styles.name: Arnold Böcklin
styles.features: Dark cypress groves on rocky islands; still black water; white-shrouded figures; deep greens and Prussian blues; tritons, nereids and centaurs among green waves; solid modelling and theatrical light.

styles.name: Franz von Stuck
styles.features: Gleaming pale figures and serpents against near-black backgrounds; sharp sculptural modelling; smooth enamel-like surface; gold and deep red accents; classical myth in theatrical darkness, often within painted architectural frames.

styles.name: Max Klinger
styles.features: Precise etched lines and aquatint tones in black and white; dreamlike sequential scenes where realistic interiors and landscapes are invaded by uncanny events; crisp academic drawing with wide paper margins.

styles.name: Gustav Klimt, golden period
styles.medium: oil with gold and silver leaf on canvas
styles.features: Flat golden fields of applied leaf filled with spirals, eyes, rectangles and mosaic-like ornament; softly modelled realistic faces and hands emerging from patterned robes; square landscapes dense with flowers.

styles.name: Ferdinand Hodler
styles.features: Rhythmic repetition of similar figures in symmetrical rows; firm dark contour lines; flat horizontal bands of lake, mountain and sky; clear cool blues and whites; stylised gestures and simplified planes.

styles.name: Edvard Munch
styles.features: Flowing undulating contours; simplified mask-like faces; flat blood reds, deep blues and acid yellow-greens; thin scraped paint; Nordic shorelines with a moon's column of light on water; isolated anxious figures.

styles.name: Vilhelm Hammershøi
styles.features: Muted grey, white and pale ochre interiors; closed doors and bare floorboards; soft window light; a woman in black seen from behind; hazy brushed texture; nearly empty rooms of complete stillness.

styles.name: Harald Sohlberg
styles.features: Clear twilight skies glowing turquoise and pale gold above dark blue mountains; sharply silhouetted pines; snowfields; symmetrical stillness; a few lit windows or a single star; Nordic summer-night colour.

styles.name: Hugo Simberg
styles.features: Deliberately naive simple drawing; small sullen angels, kindly devils and skeleton Death figures in the Finnish countryside; muted earthy browns, greens and greys; flat watercolour with folk-tale humour and melancholy.

styles.name: Akseli Gallen-Kallela
styles.medium: oil and tempera on canvas; fresco
styles.features: Bold dark contours and flat clear colour areas; heroic figures from Finnish epic poetry; Karelian wilderness of rapids, rocks, pines and frozen lakes; folk-ornament borders; crisp tempera clarity.

styles.name: Agnes Slott-Møller
styles.features: Medieval Danish ballad and saga subjects; stiff upright figures in richly patterned medieval costume; clear outlines and strong flat colour; Danish heaths and coasts; decorative framing in tapestry-like compositions.

styles.name: Hilma af Klint
styles.medium: oil and tempera on paper mounted on canvas
styles.features: Large flat diagrams in pastel pink, ochre, lavender and blue; spirals, petals, circles, swan and snail-shell forms; symmetrical botanical-geometric symbols; letters and cursive words floating on flat grounds.
styles.note: Abstract; use for cosmic, spiritual or growth themes rather than literal scenes

styles.name: Mikalojus Konstantinas Čiurlionis
styles.features: Thin translucent tempera in pale blue, green and amber; dreamlike cosmic landscapes of pyramids, towers, waves and starry skies arranged like musical sequences; soft edges, misty layered planes, small symbolic figures.

styles.name: Mikhail Vrubel
styles.features: Faceted crystalline brushstrokes like mosaic or broken gemstones; deep violet, lilac, turquoise and pearl; brooding figures with enormous eyes; Russian fairy-tale and demonic subjects; shimmering ornament.

styles.name: Mikhail Nesterov
styles.features: Thin young birches; pale spring or autumn northern landscapes; still rivers and wooden monasteries; quiet monks, hermits and devout women in the foreground; cool silvery light, muted greens and greys.

styles.name: Nicholas Roerich
styles.features: Flat tempera in saturated blues, violets and reds; simplified massive mountain ranges and stylised clouds; ancient Slavic hills, wooden towns, Viking boats, Himalayan monasteries; small figures within calm outlined colour planes.

styles.name: Konstantin Somov, Mir iskusstva
styles.features: Delicate watercolour and gouache; rococo ladies and gentlemen in powdered wigs; rainbows, fireworks, lanterns and garden pavilions at dusk; porcelain-like miniature figures; pastel pinks and greens with ironic charm.

styles.name: Jacek Malczewski
styles.features: Crisp realist painting of Polish peasants and fields combined with fantastic beings—fauns, chimeras, angels in peasant clothes; bright clear colour, sharp daylight and dense allegorical groupings.

styles.name: Stanisław Wyspiański
styles.features: Pastel with strong contour lines and flat colour; wild flowers and plants treated as sinuous linear ornament; children's portraits and Kraków views; stained-glass figures and tendrils in blazing colour.

styles.name: Albert Pinkham Ryder
styles.medium: oil on canvas, thick layered paint
styles.features: Thick layered cracked paint; dark brown and olive tonal seas; moonlit sailboats under bulging luminous clouds; simplified blocky forms; glowing yellow moon; sombre visionary mood with minimal detail.

styles.name: Alphonse Mucha
styles.features: Young women with swirling stylised hair set within halo-like circular frames; mosaic and floral ornament; smooth clear outlines; soft pastel colours; Byzantine-style jewellery and flowing robes.
styles.note: Use the decorative-panel format without lettering

styles.name: Gustav Klimt, golden phase
styles.medium: oil with gold and silver leaf on canvas
styles.features: Naturalistically modelled faces and hands emerging from flat fields of gold leaf, garments patterned with spirals, eye-shapes, rectangles and mosaic squares, flattened space without horizon, ochre, gold, black accents
styles.section: Art Nouveau, Vienna Secession, Jugendstil, Arts and Crafts — painting, graphics and decorative art

styles.name: Gustav Klimt, square-format landscapes
styles.features: Square canvases with high or absent horizon, meadows, orchards and lake shores built from dense dabs of colour like tapestry, flower-sprinkled grass, upright tree trunks, flat decorative space, greens and blues
styles.section: Art Nouveau, Vienna Secession, Jugendstil, Arts and Crafts — painting, graphics and decorative art
styles.note: The name alone may trigger the gold-figure look; rely on the features

styles.name: Egon Schiele
styles.medium: gouache, watercolour and pencil on paper
styles.features: Angular contorted figures drawn with a nervous wiry contour, gaunt limbs and knotted hands, patchy washes of ochre, rust and green on bare paper, also tightly packed crooked townhouse facades
styles.section: Art Nouveau, Vienna Secession, Jugendstil, Arts and Crafts — painting, graphics and decorative art
styles.note: Nudes dominate his work; specify clothed figures

styles.name: Koloman Moser
styles.features: Strictly symmetrical compositions, stylised maidens or flowers repeated in rhythmic rows, flat unmodulated colour, black-and-white chequerboard motifs, square and circle ornament, geometric framing of every element
styles.section: Art Nouveau, Vienna Secession, Jugendstil, Arts and Crafts — painting, graphics and decorative art

styles.name: Wiener Werkstätte decorative arts
styles.medium: silver, enamel, lacquer, printed textile, postcards
styles.features: Rigorous grids of small black-and-white squares, pierced square-lattice metal baskets, white surfaces with black edging, cubic furniture; later textiles with dense small stylised flowers in bright flat colours
styles.section: Art Nouveau, Vienna Secession, Jugendstil, Arts and Crafts — painting, graphics and decorative art

styles.name: Vienna Secession exhibition poster
styles.features: Tall narrow format, blocky geometric hand-drawn lettering fused with image, large areas of empty paper, flat colour fields in two or three tones, stylised figure or square ornament, rigid frames
styles.section: Art Nouveau, Vienna Secession, Jugendstil, Arts and Crafts — painting, graphics and decorative art

styles.name: William Morris
styles.features: Dense symmetrical repeat patterns of acanthus, willow boughs, honeysuckle and birds among interlacing stems, flat outlined forms, indigo, madder red, weld yellow and olive vegetable-dye palette
styles.section: Art Nouveau, Vienna Secession, Jugendstil, Arts and Crafts — painting, graphics and decorative art

styles.name: Kelmscott Press book page
styles.medium: wood-engraved borders and type on handmade paper
styles.features: Heavy black vine-and-leaf borders filling the margins, large decorated initials, dense Gothic-roman type in black and red, medievalising woodcut illustrations with knights and maidens, white leaves on black ground
styles.section: Art Nouveau, Vienna Secession, Jugendstil, Arts and Crafts — painting, graphics and decorative art

styles.name: Walter Crane
styles.features: Firm black outlines, flat clear colours with Japanese-print flatness, classical and medieval costumes, figures arranged in friezes, patterned floors and wallpapers, decorative borders around the scene
styles.section: Art Nouveau, Vienna Secession, Jugendstil, Arts and Crafts — painting, graphics and decorative art

styles.name: Eugène Grasset
styles.medium: colour lithograph poster, stained glass design
styles.features: Heavy black cloisonné outlines like leaded glass, flat muted greens, ochres and blues, medievalising women in gardens and fields, stylised plants, integrated decorative lettering
styles.section: Art Nouveau, Vienna Secession, Jugendstil, Arts and Crafts — painting, graphics and decorative art

styles.name: Théophile-Alexandre Steinlen
styles.features: Bold flat silhouettes, sketchy crayon texture, warm oranges, ochres and blacks, cats in elegant poses, Montmartre street scenes with workers, laundresses and passers-by
styles.section: Art Nouveau, Vienna Secession, Jugendstil, Arts and Crafts — painting, graphics and decorative art

styles.name: Jules Chéret
styles.features: Whirling joyful young women in motion, loose sketchy drawing, airy transparent layers of bright red, yellow and blue blending into light backgrounds, large lively lettering
styles.section: Art Nouveau, Vienna Secession, Jugendstil, Arts and Crafts — painting, graphics and decorative art

styles.name: Manuel Orazi
styles.features: Tall narrow panels, pale women in heavy embroidered robes and jewellery, occult and Byzantine ornament, dense gold accents, deep greens and dark reds, flat Japanese-inspired composition
styles.section: Art Nouveau, Vienna Secession, Jugendstil, Arts and Crafts — painting, graphics and decorative art

styles.name: Privat-Livemont
styles.features: Women with long flowing hair separated from the background by a pale white outline halo, soft pastel colours, floral arabesques, curling smoke and whiplash motifs, ornate lettering panels
styles.section: Art Nouveau, Vienna Secession, Jugendstil, Arts and Crafts — painting, graphics and decorative art

styles.name: Louis Comfort Tiffany
styles.features: Streaky opalescent and iridescent glass, rippled drapery glass, copper-foil lead lines as drawing, wisteria, magnolias, rivers and sunsets, gradients from violet to amber, glowing lamp shades
styles.section: Art Nouveau, Vienna Secession, Jugendstil, Arts and Crafts — painting, graphics and decorative art
styles.note: Use the full name to avoid the jewellery brand

styles.name: Émile Gallé
styles.features: Layered translucent glass etched in relief, dragonflies, orchids, thistles and night moths, amber, violet and moss-green over frosted grounds, glowing from within
styles.section: Art Nouveau, Vienna Secession, Jugendstil, Arts and Crafts — painting, graphics and decorative art

styles.name: Art Nouveau jewellery, Paris, plique-à-jour enamel
styles.features: Translucent enamel set without backing like tiny stained glass, dragonfly wings, insect-woman brooches, orchids and poppies, baroque pearls and opals, sinuous gold tendrils
styles.section: Art Nouveau, Vienna Secession, Jugendstil, Arts and Crafts — painting, graphics and decorative art

styles.name: Hector Guimard
styles.features: Green-painted cast iron shaped like plant stems, bud-like lamps, fan-shaped glass canopies, curving irregular frames, asymmetrical brick and stone facades with organic ironwork
styles.section: Art Nouveau, Vienna Secession, Jugendstil, Arts and Crafts — painting, graphics and decorative art

styles.name: Antoni Gaudí
styles.features: Undulating walls and roofs, bone-like balconies, twisted columns, broken glazed tile mosaic in bright blues, greens and ochres, swirling chimneys, organic forms with no straight lines
styles.section: Art Nouveau, Vienna Secession, Jugendstil, Arts and Crafts — painting, graphics and decorative art

styles.name: Victor Horta
styles.medium: architecture, wrought iron, mosaic, wall painting
styles.features: Open stairwells under glass skylights, iron columns splitting into whiplash tendrils, curving lines repeated in railings, mosaic floors and painted walls, warm wood, cream, gold-green
styles.section: Art Nouveau, Vienna Secession, Jugendstil, Arts and Crafts — painting, graphics and decorative art

styles.name: Charles Rennie Mackintosh
styles.features: Tall high-backed chairs with ladder slats, rectangular lattices, stylised Glasgow rose, white-painted rooms with mauve, pink and silver accents, strong verticals; flower watercolours with precise outlines
styles.section: Art Nouveau, Vienna Secession, Jugendstil, Arts and Crafts — painting, graphics and decorative art

styles.name: Jessie M. King
styles.medium: pen and ink with pale watercolour on vellum
styles.features: Extremely fine wiry pen line, tiny dots and stars, slender pale figures, fragile castles and thin trees, generous white space, delicate washes of pale rose, green and gold
styles.section: Art Nouveau, Vienna Secession, Jugendstil, Arts and Crafts — painting, graphics and decorative art

styles.name: Otto Eckmann
styles.features: Flat Japanese-influenced woodcut, swans gliding on rippled water, flowing parallel lines, soft greens, blues and ochres, stylised irises and reeds, decorative curving forms
styles.section: Art Nouveau, Vienna Secession, Jugendstil, Arts and Crafts — painting, graphics and decorative art

styles.name: Jugend magazine cover, Munich
styles.features: Hand-drawn masthead integrated with illustration, flat bright colours, whimsical stylised figures, flowing outlines, floral ornament and playful decorative borders
styles.section: Art Nouveau, Vienna Secession, Jugendstil, Arts and Crafts — painting, graphics and decorative art

styles.name: Heinrich Vogeler
styles.features: Slender maidens and knights among birches and blossoming gardens, fine detailed line, delicate spring greens and whites, ornamental arched frames, quiet fairy-tale rural Worpswede scenery
styles.section: Art Nouveau, Vienna Secession, Jugendstil, Arts and Crafts — painting, graphics and decorative art

styles.name: Ivan Bilibin
styles.features: Crisp black ink contours filled with flat watercolour, ornate frame borders of Russian folk motifs, fairy-tale costumes, dense spruce forests, carved wooden izbas, stylised clouds and waves
styles.section: Art Nouveau, Vienna Secession, Jugendstil, Arts and Crafts — painting, graphics and decorative art

styles.name: Elena Polenova
styles.features: Russian fairy-tale illustrations framed with carved-wood folk ornament, muted earthy greens, browns and reds, stylised birds and plants, Abramtsevo carved cabinets and shelves
styles.section: Art Nouveau, Vienna Secession, Jugendstil, Arts and Crafts — painting, graphics and decorative art

styles.name: Talashkino workshops
styles.medium: carved and painted wood, embroidery, enamel
styles.features: Chip-carved furniture and balalaikas painted with firebirds, suns and stylised animals, bold neo-folk ornament, deep reds, greens and blues, heavy embroidered borders
styles.section: Art Nouveau, Vienna Secession, Jugendstil, Arts and Crafts — painting, graphics and decorative art

styles.name: Gerhard Munthe
styles.features: Flat symmetrical folk-tale scenes, stylised trolls, riders and animals, interlaced dragon-head ornament, broad bands of rust red, indigo and yellow, strong outlines
styles.section: Art Nouveau, Vienna Secession, Jugendstil, Arts and Crafts — painting, graphics and decorative art

styles.name: Frida Hansen
styles.features: Tapestries with areas of bare unwoven warp letting light through, stylised maidens, flowers and fruit in flat bright reds, blues and yellows, rhythmic repetitive figures
styles.section: Art Nouveau, Vienna Secession, Jugendstil, Arts and Crafts — painting, graphics and decorative art

styles.name: Riga Art Nouveau facades
styles.features: Tall apartment facades in pastel plaster, giant screaming masks, lions and peacocks, blue glazed brick panels, bay windows, stylised plant reliefs, steep gables
styles.section: Art Nouveau, Vienna Secession, Jugendstil, Arts and Crafts — painting, graphics and decorative art

styles.name: Hungarian Secession, Zsolnay eosin ceramics
styles.features: Iridescent metallic eosin glaze shifting green, red and gold, Hungarian folk floral motifs, multicoloured patterned roof tiles, vases with stylised flowers
styles.section: Art Nouveau, Vienna Secession, Jugendstil, Arts and Crafts — painting, graphics and decorative art

styles.name: Will Bradley
styles.features: Flat red, black and cream, bold silhouettes, repeated stylised figures, heavy decorative typography, mix of Beardsley-like line and Arts and Crafts woodcut borders
styles.section: Art Nouveau, Vienna Secession, Jugendstil, Arts and Crafts — painting, graphics and decorative art

styles.name: Ethel Reed
styles.features: Flat Japanese-influenced colour areas, young women in large hats, poppies or roses, limited palette of greens, reds and black, strong silhouettes
styles.section: Art Nouveau, Vienna Secession, Jugendstil, Arts and Crafts — painting, graphics and decorative art

styles.name: William De Morgan
styles.features: Ruby and copper lustre, Iznik-inspired turquoise and cobalt, fantastical beasts, ships, fish and birds fitted into circular dishes or tile repeats, glossy surface
styles.section: Art Nouveau, Vienna Secession, Jugendstil, Arts and Crafts — painting, graphics and decorative art

styles.name: C. F. A. Voysey
styles.features: Light open grounds, flat simple outlines, birds in rows, hearts, rounded trees and flowers, airy spacing, soft greens, blues and creams
styles.section: Art Nouveau, Vienna Secession, Jugendstil, Arts and Crafts — painting, graphics and decorative art

styles.name: American Craftsman interior, Mission style
styles.medium: quartersawn oak, hammered copper, leaded glass, mica
styles.features: Heavy straight oak furniture with exposed joinery, built-in benches, mica lamp shades, hammered copper, leaded glass, earthy greens, browns and amber
styles.section: Art Nouveau, Vienna Secession, Jugendstil, Arts and Crafts — painting, graphics and decorative art

styles.name: Newcomb College Pottery
styles.features: Matte blue-green glazes, carved low relief, live oaks hung with Spanish moss, rising moon, stylised irises and magnolias, bands of repeated trees around the vase
styles.section: Art Nouveau, Vienna Secession, Jugendstil, Arts and Crafts — painting, graphics and decorative art

styles.name: Arthur Wesley Dow
styles.features: Flat tonal masses in light and dark arrangement, few soft colours, salt marshes, rivers and coastal hills, simplified trees, Japanese-print composition
styles.section: Art Nouveau, Vienna Secession, Jugendstil, Arts and Crafts — painting, graphics and decorative art

styles.name: Archibald Knox
styles.features: Celtic knotwork, stylised honesty leaves, smooth hammered pewter and silver, turquoise and blue-green enamel insets, clocks, vessels and boxes
styles.section: Art Nouveau, Vienna Secession, Jugendstil, Arts and Crafts — painting, graphics and decorative art

styles.name: Hermann Obrist
styles.features: Single plant stem with roots and flowers whipping into a dramatic looping curve, gold-yellow silk on dark ground, dynamic energy, mostly abstracted
styles.section: Art Nouveau, Vienna Secession, Jugendstil, Arts and Crafts — painting, graphics and decorative art

styles.name: Alexandre de Riquer
styles.features: Thin precise outlines, pale greens and golds, women among flowers, decorative frames, intricate bookplates
styles.section: Art Nouveau, Vienna Secession, Jugendstil, Arts and Crafts — painting, graphics and decorative art

styles.name: Galileo Chini
styles.features: Byzantine gold grounds, peacocks and stylised flowers, iridescent lustre vases, Southeast Asian ornament, flat decorative figures in golds, blues and reds
styles.section: Art Nouveau, Vienna Secession, Jugendstil, Arts and Crafts — painting, graphics and decorative art

styles.name: May Morris
styles.features: Dense embroidered honeysuckle, fruit trees and birds, long-and-short stitch shading, soft muted greens, golds and pinks on natural linen ground
styles.section: Art Nouveau, Vienna Secession, Jugendstil, Arts and Crafts — painting, graphics and decorative art

styles.name: Maurice Pillard Verneuil
styles.features: Stylised plants, insects and animals arranged as repeating patterns, flat stencilled colour with soft gradients, systematic pattern-book plates
styles.section: Art Nouveau, Vienna Secession, Jugendstil, Arts and Crafts — painting, graphics and decorative art

styles.name: Élisabeth Sonrel
styles.features: Women in medievalising gowns, delicate drawing, garlands of flowers, soft pinks, golds and greens, decorative halos and borders
styles.section: Art Nouveau, Vienna Secession, Jugendstil, Arts and Crafts — painting, graphics and decorative art

styles.name: Henri Matisse, Fauve period
styles.features: Flat patches of pure unmixed colour used arbitrarily: green shadows on faces, red trees, violet skies. Loose quick brushstrokes, bare canvas left showing, simplified outlined figures, open windows onto harbours.

styles.name: André Derain
styles.features: Mosaic of broad separate strokes in saturated colour, with yellow rivers, cobalt shadows, vermilion boats and pink-orange skies. White ground glimpsed between dabs, high viewpoint over harbours and bridges, flattened depth.

styles.name: Maurice de Vlaminck, Fauve period
styles.features: Thick paint applied straight from the tube in swirling, comma-like strokes of vermilion, cobalt and chrome yellow. Riverside villages, trees and tugboats vibrate with energy, and dark lines rim the houses and trunks.

styles.name: Raoul Dufy
styles.medium: oil on canvas, watercolour and gouache on paper
styles.features: Transparent washes of bright blue, red and green that spill beyond a quick, calligraphic black ink drawing. Regattas, racecourses, orchestras and seaside promenades are shown with many tiny lively figures, flags and white sails.

styles.name: Albert Marquet
styles.features: Harbours, quays and bridges seen from a high window, with forms simplified into flat calm planes of grey-blue water and ochre stone. Boats, passers-by and trams are suggested by a few quick dark calligraphic touches, under a soft, diffuse light.

styles.name: Kees van Dongen
styles.features: Elegant women with enlarged almond eyes rimmed in black, scarlet lips and acid green or blue shadows on pale skin. Flat saturated backgrounds, harsh electric light, and loose fluid strokes for gowns and feathered hats.

styles.name: Henri Manguin
styles.features: Warm sunlit Mediterranean gardens and terraces, with orange, rose, violet and emerald laid on in broad, loose, juicy strokes. Women reading or resting in dappled shade, and foliage and figures merge into a glowing decorative surface.

styles.name: Louis Valtat
styles.features: Short thick parallel strokes of hot colour: red-orange coastal rocks, purple and turquoise sea, blazing yellow light. Coastlines, gardens and flower bouquets are built from rhythmic dashes with little modelling and a high horizon.

styles.name: Émilie Charmy
styles.features: Thick, fluid, sensuous brushwork in warm reds, ochres and creamy whites. Women at their toilette, flower vases and intimate interiors are shown with forms half-dissolving in light, outlines loose and backgrounds roughly scumbled.

styles.name: Jacqueline Marval
styles.features: Decorative compositions of elongated reclining women set against patterned fabrics and flowers. Pale pinks, turquoise and lemon are held in firm dark contours, with flattened space, stylised faces and a frieze-like arrangement of figures.

styles.name: Georges Rouault
styles.medium: oil on paper and canvas, heavy layered impasto
styles.features: Thick black contours like the lead lines of stained glass, enclosing glowing jewel colours of deep blue, crimson and gold. Paint is crusted and layered. Clowns, kings, judges and sorrowful faces are frontal and heavy.

styles.name: Georges Braque, Fauve period
styles.features: Mediterranean hills, harbours and houses in pinks, violets, oranges and turquoise, built from curving strokes and small dabs. Shapes are bounded by light blue or purple lines, with a growing sense of solid structure beneath the colour.

styles.name: Ernst Ludwig Kirchner
styles.features: Jagged, hatched brushstrokes and acid pink, green and violet. Elongated angular figures with mask-like faces crowd steeply tilted city streets. Later work shows Alpine peaks and peasants in flat bright patches.

styles.name: Erich Heckel
styles.features: Crystalline, faceted forms as if cut from wood, with prism-like shafts of light. Pale greens, ochres and chalky blues sit within dark angular contours. Gaunt bathers, sick rooms and coastal landscapes are shown with sharp splintered shapes.

styles.name: Karl Schmidt-Rottluff
styles.features: Massive blocky shapes in loud flat colour, with crimson, ultramarine, emerald and orange side by side and few transitions. Heavy black outlines, villages and dunes reduced to slabs, faces simplified into carved masks.

styles.name: Max Pechstein
styles.features: Warm oranges, ochres and greens in flat outlined shapes with rhythmic decorative contours. Fishermen hauling boats, bathers on beaches and lagoon shores have strong bodies drawn with bold dark lines and simplified features.
styles.note: Render bathers clothed or in swimwear.

styles.name: Emil Nolde
styles.medium: oil on canvas; watercolour on Japan paper
styles.features: Glowing wet-in-wet watercolour where blooms of colour bleed into soft absorbent paper, with poppies and dahlias in fiery reds and deep violets. Stormy seas and blood-red skies. In oils, thick grotesque mask-like faces.

styles.name: Otto Mueller
styles.features: Matte chalky glue-tempera on rough sacking with the weave visible. Muted ochre, sage green and pale terracotta. Slender angular figures with almond eyes among reeds, dunes and ponds, softly outlined in dark brown.
styles.note: Render figures clothed.

styles.name: German Expressionist woodcut
styles.features: Gouged, splintered black shapes against raw white paper, with wood grain and knife marks visible. Angular distorted figures, mask-like faces, harsh contrasts and almost no mid-tones. Occasional single flat colour block printed in red or ochre.

styles.name: Franz Marc
styles.features: Animals in pure symbolic colour, such as blue horses, yellow cows and red deer, with rounded rhythmic bodies curling into the landscape. Prism-like intersecting planes cut the space and hills echo animal curves.

styles.name: Wassily Kandinsky, Murnau period
styles.features: Village houses, church towers and mountain roads dissolving into thick strokes of glowing blue, orange, yellow and green. Forms are flattened and outlined loosely, and horse riders and figures are reduced to colour signs.
styles.note: Specify the pre-abstract landscape phase to avoid pure abstraction.

styles.name: Gabriele Münter
styles.features: Flat unmodulated fields of colour enclosed by dark outlines, like folk reverse-glass painting. Murnau houses, mountain lanes, interiors and still lifes with folk carvings, in deep blue, green, mustard and red under clear simplified light.

styles.name: August Macke
styles.features: Luminous transparent colour planes in harmonious orange, turquoise, lemon and rose. Strollers in hats beside shop windows and park lakes, with figures simplified without faces. Light faceting of space into gently overlapping prismatic shapes.

styles.name: Alexej von Jawlensky
styles.features: Frontal heads with huge dark eyes framed by heavy blue-black contours. Faces are built from intense flat patches of red, green, orange and violet, with icon-like stillness against simplified backgrounds.

styles.name: Marianne von Werefkin
styles.medium: tempera and gouache on paper and cardboard
styles.features: Dramatic scenes under luminous unreal skies of pink, ultramarine and acid green. Small dark figures walk long winding roads, and mountains, houses and lamps are simplified into flat glowing shapes with theatrical mood.

styles.name: Heinrich Campendonk
styles.medium: oil on canvas, reverse painting on glass
styles.features: Dreamlike rural scenes with cows, goats, harlequins and peasants arranged frontally in flat interlocking planes. Jewel-like reds, greens and blues sit within dark outlines. Folk-glass flatness and fairy-tale stillness.

styles.name: Lyonel Feininger
styles.features: Gothic village churches, sailing ships and streets broken into transparent crystalline planes. Ruled lines and shafts of light overlap like prisms in cool blues, ochres and violets, with tiny elongated figures.

styles.name: Paula Modersohn-Becker
styles.medium: oil and tempera on canvas and board
styles.features: Simplified heavy figures of peasant women and children, frontal and monumental, with large dark eyes. A matte, dry surface in earthy browns, moss greens and terracotta. Still lifes with fruit and flowers in plain, solid forms.
styles.note: Render figures clothed.

styles.name: Oskar Kokoschka
styles.features: Restless, scratched and flickering brushwork with feverish colour. Psychological portraits stress twitching hands. Later, panoramic city and river views from a height are churned with swirling strokes of blue, green and orange.

styles.name: Ludwig Meidner
styles.features: Apocalyptic cityscapes with buildings tilting and collapsing, streets cracking into jagged diagonals and exploding skies with comets and fire. Tiny fleeing crowds, harsh yellows, reds and inky blues, frenzied strokes.

styles.name: Käthe Kollwitz
styles.medium: lithograph, etching, woodcut and charcoal on paper
styles.features: Black-and-white images with deep shadow and rough grainy strokes. Workers, mothers and children are shown with heavy hands and bowed heads, sculptural in their simplicity, grouped in tight masses with sparse settings.

styles.name: Max Beckmann
styles.features: Thick black outlines around solid figures crammed into shallow, compressed spaces. Saturated violet, orange, green and black. Masked revellers, actors and mythic figures in claustrophobic stage-like interiors with flattened, tilted perspective.

styles.name: Christian Rohlfs
styles.features: Layered thin translucent colour, rubbed and washed until forms glow and dissolve. Flowers, church towers and small-town streets appear in luminous reds, violets and golds, with soft edges and floating light.

styles.name: Conrad Felixmüller
styles.features: Sharp-edged angular forms and cubist-inflected faceting with strong light-dark contrasts. Miners, steelworkers and families in industrial towns appear among smokestacks and pitheads, with figures drawn with emphatic outlines.

styles.name: Lovis Corinth, late period
styles.features: Violent smeared brushwork with paint dragged and slashed until forms half-dissolve. Mountain lake landscapes in intense blues and greens, flower still lifes and portraits loosely built from thick, agitated strokes.

styles.name: Sigrid Hjertén
styles.features: Bold flat colour and decorative patterning. Views over harbours and bridges from a high studio window, plus interiors with women and children. Strong reds, greens and blues, with simplified, slightly naïve figures.

styles.name: Isaac Grünewald
styles.features: Decorative, rhythmic compositions in bright saturated colour. Harbour views, bridges and city lights appear in sweeping curves and flat bands of blue, orange and green, with elongated figures and lively outlines.

styles.name: Tyko Sallinen
styles.features: Rough, vigorous brushwork and simplified angular forms in earthy ochres, reds and dark greens. Finnish villagers, washerwomen and fervent revival-meeting dancers rendered with crude energy against stark rural landscapes.

styles.name: Helene Schjerfbeck
styles.medium: oil on canvas, scraped and sanded
styles.features: Pared-down portraits with faces reduced to quiet masks. Surfaces are scraped, sanded and repainted. Muted greys, chalky whites, ochre and a single accent of red, with sparse still lifes of a few fruits.

styles.name: Jón Stefánsson
styles.features: Icelandic mountains, lava fields and grazing horses built in solid, constructive planes of colour. Cool blues and violets set against ochre and moss green, with clear structured volumes and broad, flat, quiet spaces.

styles.name: Ludvig Karsten
styles.features: Vehement broad strokes in saturated blues, reds and yellows. Kitchens, rooms and figures are dissolved into rapid sweeps of colour, with loose, energetic handling and objects only suggested.

styles.name: Konrad Mägi
styles.features: Glowing, unnaturally vivid landscapes of rolling hills, lakes and juniper shores. Decorative rhythms of dotted and swirling strokes, with intense violet, emerald, orange and gold under luminous skies.

styles.name: Natalia Goncharova, Neo-primitivism
styles.features: Peasants harvesting, dancing and fishing, with bold flat colour and heavy black outlines drawn from icons and lubok prints. Massive simplified bodies, rhythmic gestures, and strong reds, yellows and greens.

styles.name: Ilya Mashkov
styles.features: Loud still lifes of loaves, pumpkins, fruit and flowers heaped on patterned cloths. Glossy saturated colour, thick dark contours and robust sculptural volumes in a crowded, festive abundance.

styles.name: Aristarkh Lentulov
styles.medium: oil on canvas with paper and foil collage
styles.features: Moscow churches and onion domes shattered into fragmented, tilted planes. Red, gold, green and blue with glittering foil accents. Kaleidoscopic swirling composition and a festive sense of bells ringing.

styles.name: Chaim Soutine
styles.features: Convulsive thick paint with writhing strokes. Hillside villages heave and twist, trees bend, and still lifes of fish and fowl glow with blood-red and deep blue on dark grounds, contorted portraits.
styles.note: Avoid carcass imagery; use fish, fowl or landscapes.

styles.name: James Ensor
styles.features: Swarming crowds of grotesque carnival masks and skeletons. Acid pinks, greens and white with scratchy nervous line and palette-knife paint. Flattened jostling space and caricatured faces.

styles.name: Constant Permeke
styles.features: Massive, heavy figures of fishermen and farmers rendered in thick, earthy paint in browns, dark greens and rust. Monumental forms filling the frame, grey-green seas, and dense, muddy flat fields.

styles.name: Gustave De Smet
styles.features: Village fairs, cafés and couples with rounded, doll-like simplified figures. Warm palette of brown-red, ochre and muted blue, flattened interlocking planes, and gentle stillness with stage-like settings.

styles.name: Jan Sluijters
styles.features: Vivid strokes and broken dots of saturated colour. Moonlit landscapes in violet and yellow, and lively figures and dance halls built from bold dashes of pure pigment with strong light effects.

styles.name: Marsden Hartley, Maine period
styles.features: Heavy black outlines around massive rocks, crashing waves, pines and burly fishermen. Coarse thick paint, dark blues, browns and white surf, with blunt simplified forms and dense heavy compositions.

styles.name: Scottish Colourists, Edinburgh
styles.features: Fluid, confident brushwork with bright still lifes of tulips, fruit and Chinese vases. Black accent outlines, turquoise seas and white sand beaches, plus elegant interiors in saturated pink, orange and green.

styles.name: Anita Malfatti
styles.features: Distorted portraits with yellow-green and blue faces, bold rough strokes and flat backgrounds. Elongated figures with expressive staring eyes, set against strong contrasts of vivid tropical colours.

styles.name: Yūzō Saeki
styles.features: Paris shopfronts and peeling walls seen head-on, with nervous calligraphic black line scrawled over posters and signs. Greys, ochres and dirty whites with a few bright accents, thick dragged paint.
styles.note: Lettering on walls should stay illegible scrawls.

styles.name: German Expressionist film set design, 1920s
styles.medium: painted canvas and wood film sets, black-and-white film
styles.features: Crooked buildings with slanting walls and jagged windows. Shadows and light streaks painted directly onto sets, zigzag streets, stark black, white and sepia tones, and stylised figures in theatrical poses.

styles.name: Pablo Picasso, Cubist period
styles.features: Figures, guitars, bottles and café tables broken into small overlapping translucent facets in shallow space, muted browns, ochres and greys; later flat interlocking coloured planes, faces combining profile and frontal views
styles.section: Cubism, Futurism, Orphism, Vorticism, Rayonism and related early avant-garde
styles.note: Specify the Cubist period, not the Blue or Rose periods

styles.name: Georges Braque
styles.medium: oil on canvas with sand, papier collé
styles.features: Still lifes of violins, guitars, jugs and fruit bowls broken into interpenetrating planes, earthy ochre, olive and grey palette, faux wood grain, gritty sanded texture, stencilled letters, space tipping toward the viewer
styles.section: Cubism, Futurism, Orphism, Vorticism, Rayonism and related early avant-garde

styles.name: Juan Gris
styles.features: Crisp Synthetic Cubism: flat interlocking planes with sharp edges, deep blues, blacks and warm browns, objects shown as silhouette and shadow at once, table still lifes by open windows, checkerboard and wood-grain patches
styles.section: Cubism, Futurism, Orphism, Vorticism, Rayonism and related early avant-garde

styles.name: Fernand Léger
styles.features: Tubular cylindrical figures and machine parts with bold black outlines, primary red, yellow and blue beside white highlights and metallic grey shading, flat colour bands, workers, cyclists, acrobats and stacked mechanical city forms
styles.section: Cubism, Futurism, Orphism, Vorticism, Rayonism and related early avant-garde

styles.name: Albert Gleizes
styles.features: Large Cubist scenes of harvests, bathers and cities built from broad rhythmic angular planes, curved arcs crossing straight edges, earthy greens, browns and grey-blues, landscape and figures merged through multiple viewpoints
styles.section: Cubism, Futurism, Orphism, Vorticism, Rayonism and related early avant-garde

styles.name: Jean Metzinger
styles.features: Elegant women, cyclists, horses and café scenes split into geometric facets, patches of dotted mosaic-like brushwork, smooth faceted faces with simultaneous profile views, harmonious pastels and greys arranged on a decorative grid of planes
styles.section: Cubism, Futurism, Orphism, Vorticism, Rayonism and related early avant-garde

styles.name: Robert Delaunay
styles.features: Orphism: concentric circular discs and arcs of pure prismatic colour, contrasting hues set side by side, the Eiffel Tower and city windows fractured into bending, toppling facets, light rendered entirely through colour, rotating rhythm
styles.section: Cubism, Futurism, Orphism, Vorticism, Rayonism and related early avant-garde

styles.name: Sonia Delaunay
styles.medium: oil, gouache, printed and appliquéd textiles
styles.features: Simultaneous contrasts: interlocking circles, half-discs, squares and stripes in saturated red, orange, blue, green and black, flat colour fields, patchwork textile patterns, dancers and lamplit boulevards dissolved into rhythms of colour
styles.section: Cubism, Futurism, Orphism, Vorticism, Rayonism and related early avant-garde

styles.name: František Kupka
styles.features: Non-objective swirling discs, spirals and vertical colour bands, luminous transparent overlaps, radiating orbital rhythms, crisp edges, pinks, blues, reds and black evoking music, motion and planetary space
styles.section: Cubism, Futurism, Orphism, Vorticism, Rayonism and related early avant-garde
styles.note: Abstract; best for cosmic, musical or sky themes

styles.name: Jacques Villon
styles.features: Figures and interiors constructed through transparent pyramidal grids of fine lines, prismatic pastel planes of rose, lilac, pale green and gold, light refracted through intersecting triangles, delicate cross-hatching in prints
styles.section: Cubism, Futurism, Orphism, Vorticism, Rayonism and related early avant-garde

styles.name: Louis Marcoussis
styles.medium: oil on canvas, reverse painting on glass
styles.features: Cubist still lifes and figures with a delicate linear scaffolding, cool blues, greys and blacks, playing cards, bottles, pipes and musical instruments, fragments of lettering, smooth glossy surfaces in the glass paintings
styles.section: Cubism, Futurism, Orphism, Vorticism, Rayonism and related early avant-garde

styles.name: Roger de La Fresnaye
styles.features: Lyrical Cubism: large figures and landscapes in broad flat planes of bright blue, red and white, clear contours, simplified rounded volumes, cut-out sky patches and hills, softened geometry with legible figures, flags and balloons
styles.section: Cubism, Futurism, Orphism, Vorticism, Rayonism and related early avant-garde

styles.name: María Blanchard
styles.features: Cubist still lifes built from solid tilted planes in warm reds, ochres and deep blacks; later quiet domestic scenes of women and children with heavy simplified bodies, muted light and a melancholy stillness
styles.section: Cubism, Futurism, Orphism, Vorticism, Rayonism and related early avant-garde

styles.name: Cubist papier collé collage
styles.medium: pasted paper, newsprint and charcoal on paper
styles.features: Cut newspaper, wallpaper, faux-wood-grain paper and sheet music pasted flat, overlaid with charcoal lines drawing guitars, glasses and bottles, clean scissor edges, newsprint columns, overlapping flat shapes in beige, brown and black
styles.section: Cubism, Futurism, Orphism, Vorticism, Rayonism and related early avant-garde
styles.note: Newsprint fragments are part of the look; text can stay illegible

styles.name: Alexander Archipenko
styles.features: Elongated female figures where hollows and voids replace heads and torsos, concave forms answering convex ones, smooth polished planes, rhythmic twisting poses, painted reliefs combining wood, metal and flat colour
styles.section: Cubism, Futurism, Orphism, Vorticism, Rayonism and related early avant-garde
styles.note: Sculpture; render as a photographed object or painted relief

styles.name: Czech Cubist architecture and design, Prague
styles.features: Crystalline facades, doors and furniture folded into prismatic pyramids and diagonal facets, angular cornices and window frames, black or white glazed ceramics with sharp ribs, hard light casting star-shaped shadows
styles.section: Cubism, Futurism, Orphism, Vorticism, Rayonism and related early avant-garde

styles.name: Bohumil Kubišta
styles.features: Expressive Cubism with sharp crystalline facets, intense contrasting colour, deep blues, violets and acid yellows, dramatic diagonals, figures, harbours and Prague views broken into glowing prisms, tense mystical atmosphere
styles.section: Cubism, Futurism, Orphism, Vorticism, Rayonism and related early avant-garde

styles.name: Josef Čapek
styles.features: Simplified Cubist figures with naive, childlike charm, chunky angular shapes, heavy dark contours, sombre earth colours, flat planes, linocut contrasts of black and white, sailors, drinkers, suburban people and toys
styles.section: Cubism, Futurism, Orphism, Vorticism, Rayonism and related early avant-garde

styles.name: Umberto Boccioni
styles.features: Figures, horses and city streets dissolving into swirling force-lines and interpenetrating planes, flickering divided brushstrokes, vivid complementary colours, overlapping phases of motion, buildings tilting inward over crowds
styles.section: Cubism, Futurism, Orphism, Vorticism, Rayonism and related early avant-garde

styles.name: Giacomo Balla
styles.features: Motion shown through repeated multiplied legs, wheels, leashes and wings in sequence, iridescent interpenetrating triangular wedges of colour, speed lines, swallows' flight traced as rhythmic curves, crisp graphic precision
styles.section: Cubism, Futurism, Orphism, Vorticism, Rayonism and related early avant-garde

styles.name: Gino Severini
styles.features: Dancers and nightclub crowds fragmented into glittering mosaics of small planes, dots and stripes, bright pinks, blues and yellows, rhythmic arabesques, swirling skirts and ruffles, sequins catching light on the surface
styles.section: Cubism, Futurism, Orphism, Vorticism, Rayonism and related early avant-garde

styles.name: Carlo Carrà, Futurist period
styles.features: Turbulent crowds and street clashes in thrusting diagonals and lance-like force-lines, dark reds and blacks punctuated by flashes of light, figures merged into chaotic angular fragments, smoky urban atmosphere
styles.section: Cubism, Futurism, Orphism, Vorticism, Rayonism and related early avant-garde
styles.note: Specify the Futurist period, not his later Metaphysical work

styles.name: Luigi Russolo
styles.features: Radiating rays, repeated wave-like curves, chevrons and spiralling cones of saturated violet, blue and red, ghostly figures, trains and speeding cars, nocturnal light, sound and fog visualised as dynamic forms
styles.section: Cubism, Futurism, Orphism, Vorticism, Rayonism and related early avant-garde

styles.name: Fortunato Depero
styles.medium: oil on canvas, wool tapestry, wooden toys
styles.features: Flat toy-like geometric figures with wooden puppet bodies, mechanical dolls and stylised animals, bold saturated red, blue, yellow and black, sharp cut-out silhouettes, playful patchwork compositions resembling inlaid fabric
styles.section: Cubism, Futurism, Orphism, Vorticism, Rayonism and related early avant-garde

styles.name: Benedetta Cappa Marinetti
styles.features: Aeropainting: lands and seas seen from aircraft as swelling curved spirals, translucent layered bands of water, earth and sky, smooth luminous gradients, rhythmic undulations, soft blues, greens and golds
styles.section: Cubism, Futurism, Orphism, Vorticism, Rayonism and related early avant-garde

styles.name: Tullio Crali
styles.features: Aeropainting from inside diving aircraft: cockpit edges, plunging city grids and towers seen at vertiginous angles, sharp metallic planes, smooth airbrushed gradients in blues, greys and ochres, wings and propellers as cutting shapes
styles.section: Cubism, Futurism, Orphism, Vorticism, Rayonism and related early avant-garde

styles.name: Gerardo Dottori
styles.features: Umbrian hills, lakes and villages seen from above in luminous curving arcs, concentric hills and spiral perspective, clear blues, greens and violets, glowing light, serene aerial panoramas
styles.section: Cubism, Futurism, Orphism, Vorticism, Rayonism and related early avant-garde

styles.name: Antonio Sant'Elia
styles.features: Visionary city architecture: stepped setback towers, external lift shafts, bridges, multi-level roads and power stations drawn in thin precise ink lines, low dramatic perspective, monumental vertical masses, pale washes
styles.section: Cubism, Futurism, Orphism, Vorticism, Rayonism and related early avant-garde

styles.name: Futurist typographic poetry, parole in libertà
styles.features: Explosive pages of letters in mixed fonts and sizes scattered at angles, large onomatopoeic words, mathematical signs, arrows and diagonal rules, black ink on cream paper, battle noise and speed visualised through type
styles.section: Cubism, Futurism, Orphism, Vorticism, Rayonism and related early avant-garde
styles.note: Depends on lettering; keep words short

styles.name: Kazimir Malevich, Cubo-Futurist period
styles.features: Peasant men and women, woodcutters and village scenes built from shiny tubular cylinders and cones, metallic modelling in bright red, blue, white and ochre; later fragmented planes with stencilled letters
styles.section: Cubism, Futurism, Orphism, Vorticism, Rayonism and related early avant-garde
styles.note: Specify the Cubo-Futurist period, not Suprematism

styles.name: Lyubov Popova
styles.features: Overlapping flat and curved planes of saturated red, black, ochre and blue, hard edges with brushed textured surfaces, dynamic diagonals; earlier Cubo-Futurist figures and still lifes with lettering fragments
styles.section: Cubism, Futurism, Orphism, Vorticism, Rayonism and related early avant-garde
styles.note: Mostly abstract

styles.name: Nadezhda Udaltsova
styles.features: Cubist still lifes and seated figures in muted greys, browns and greens with bright accents, translucent intersecting planes, violins and guitars, layered geometry with a calm restrained rhythm
styles.section: Cubism, Futurism, Orphism, Vorticism, Rayonism and related early avant-garde

styles.name: Aleksandra Ekster
styles.medium: oil on canvas, gouache theatre designs
styles.features: Dynamic colour planes in vivid red, yellow, blue and black, cities fractured into glowing shards and arches; theatre costumes with bold geometric shapes, flowing fabrics and figures caught mid-gesture
styles.section: Cubism, Futurism, Orphism, Vorticism, Rayonism and related early avant-garde

styles.name: Olga Rozanova
styles.medium: oil on canvas, collage, hand-coloured prints
styles.features: Bright Cubo-Futurist cityscapes, playing cards and household objects in jagged faceted shapes, glowing pure colour against dark grounds, later translucent colour stripes, cut-paper collages with crisp edges
styles.section: Cubism, Futurism, Orphism, Vorticism, Rayonism and related early avant-garde

styles.name: Natalia Goncharova
styles.features: Neo-primitivism: peasant harvests, saints and forests drawn from icons and lubok prints, bold flat colours, thick dark outlines, heavy stylised figures, at times crossed by bright Rayonist beams of light
styles.section: Cubism, Futurism, Orphism, Vorticism, Rayonism and related early avant-garde

styles.name: Rayonism
styles.features: Canvas crossed by bundles of straight coloured rays like reflected light, intersecting diagonal strokes, glowing blues, greens, reds and yellows, objects and streets dissolved into luminous linear streams
styles.section: Cubism, Futurism, Orphism, Vorticism, Rayonism and related early avant-garde
styles.note: Near-abstract; subject should be simple

styles.name: Russian Futurist lithographed books
styles.medium: lithograph and rubber stamp on cheap paper
styles.features: Hand-lettered pages mixing scrawled script and crude primitivist drawings, smudged black ink, rough rubber-stamped letters, wallpaper or coloured paper, faceted figures, stars and animals squeezed between lines
styles.section: Cubism, Futurism, Orphism, Vorticism, Rayonism and related early avant-garde
styles.note: Depends on handwritten Cyrillic lettering

styles.name: Oleksandr Bogomazov
styles.features: Kyiv streets, trams and sawyers at work rendered in rhythmic dynamic lines and angular shards, vibrant cobalt, orange and green, vibrating energy of labour and city traffic
styles.section: Cubism, Futurism, Orphism, Vorticism, Rayonism and related early avant-garde

styles.name: Wyndham Lewis
styles.medium: oil on canvas, ink and gouache
styles.features: Vorticism: hard-edged machine-like figures, interlocking blocks and jagged diagonals, metallic greys, muted greens, ochres and pinks, crowded architectonic compositions, robot-like faces with sharp contours
styles.section: Cubism, Futurism, Orphism, Vorticism, Rayonism and related early avant-garde

styles.name: Edward Wadsworth
styles.features: Black-and-white or flat-colour woodcuts of harbours, ships and industrial towns fragmented into sharp interlocking geometric planes; later crisp tempera seashore still lifes of shells, anchors and nautical gear
styles.section: Cubism, Futurism, Orphism, Vorticism, Rayonism and related early avant-garde

styles.name: David Bomberg, early period
styles.features: Figures reduced to angular blocks and stencil-like geometric fragments, crisp planes of red, blue, cream and black, a dense grid of interlocking shapes, bustling crowds turned into near-abstract pattern
styles.section: Cubism, Futurism, Orphism, Vorticism, Rayonism and related early avant-garde
styles.note: Specify the early geometric period

styles.name: C. R. W. Nevinson
styles.features: Soldiers, machine guns, trenches and city crowds in hard angular planes, steely greys and browns, repeated marching figures, sharp diagonals, dense hatched prints, bleak wartime atmosphere
styles.section: Cubism, Futurism, Orphism, Vorticism, Rayonism and related early avant-garde

styles.name: Helen Saunders
styles.medium: ink, gouache and watercolour on paper
styles.features: Vorticist compositions of tightly packed angular shards and wedges, compressed vertical rhythms, bold pinks, ochres, blacks and greens, hints of dancing or mechanical figures inside the geometry
styles.section: Cubism, Futurism, Orphism, Vorticism, Rayonism and related early avant-garde
styles.note: Mostly abstract

styles.name: William Roberts
styles.features: Tubular muscular figures packed tightly into rhythmic groups, rounded cylindrical limbs, simplified oval faces, clear contours, warm earthy colours, everyday scenes of workers, dancers, cinema audiences and cyclists
styles.section: Cubism, Futurism, Orphism, Vorticism, Rayonism and related early avant-garde

styles.name: Henri Gaudier-Brzeska
styles.medium: carved stone, bronze, brush and ink
styles.features: Carved stone figures reduced to blocky angular masses, totemic heads and wrestlers; quick brush-and-ink drawings of animals and figures with few fluid economical lines on white paper
styles.section: Cubism, Futurism, Orphism, Vorticism, Rayonism and related early avant-garde

styles.name: Dazzle camouflage
styles.features: Ship hulls painted with bold clashing stripes, zigzags, curves and broken geometric bands in black, white, blue and grey, high-contrast patterns across funnels and decks disrupting outline and direction
styles.section: Cubism, Futurism, Orphism, Vorticism, Rayonism and related early avant-garde

styles.name: Synchromism
styles.features: Rhythmic colour abstractions of curved overlapping planes in spectral hues, faint echoes of sculptural figures, chromatic scales from warm to cool, swirling concave and convex forms, colour alone building volume
styles.section: Cubism, Futurism, Orphism, Vorticism, Rayonism and related early avant-garde
styles.note: Near-abstract

styles.name: Joseph Stella
styles.features: Bridges and skyscrapers in soaring fragmented arches, cables and girders, deep night blues with electric flashes, stained-glass-like geometric segments, vertical symmetry, whirling fairground lights
styles.section: Cubism, Futurism, Orphism, Vorticism, Rayonism and related early avant-garde

styles.name: Max Weber, Cubist period
styles.features: New York rush hours, crowds and skyscrapers fractured into dense angular rhythms, repeated geometric fragments, bright reds, blues and blacks, Cubo-Futurist energy, figures sometimes simplified into mask-like faces
styles.section: Cubism, Futurism, Orphism, Vorticism, Rayonism and related early avant-garde

styles.name: Amadeo de Souza-Cardoso
styles.features: Colliding Cubo-Futurist fragments of folk dolls, guitars, targets, cogwheels and lettering, flat saturated colour, discs and arcs, sand, mirror shards and pasted elements on the surface
styles.section: Cubism, Futurism, Orphism, Vorticism, Rayonism and related early avant-garde

styles.name: Rafael Barradas, Vibracionismo
styles.features: City streets, trams, shop fronts and passers-by broken into transparent overlapping planes with scattered numbers, warm ochres, whites and blues, flickering lively rhythm of urban movement
styles.section: Cubism, Futurism, Orphism, Vorticism, Rayonism and related early avant-garde

styles.name: Emilio Pettoruti
styles.features: Crystalline Cubist harlequins, musicians and still lifes with smooth sharply cut planes, precise geometric bands of light fanning across, luminous blues, greens and golds, serene ordered composition
styles.section: Cubism, Futurism, Orphism, Vorticism, Rayonism and related early avant-garde

styles.name: Tarsila do Amaral
styles.features: Rounded simplified figures with swollen limbs, cacti, palms and hillside houses in smooth flat colour, pinks, blues, greens and yellows, clean tubular modelling, dreamlike tropical landscapes
styles.section: Cubism, Futurism, Orphism, Vorticism, Rayonism and related early avant-garde

styles.name: Mainie Jellett
styles.features: Translucent geometric planes rotating around a central axis, soft rhythmic curves, muted rose, blue and ochre; later religious figures absorbed into the swirling geometry like stained glass
styles.section: Cubism, Futurism, Orphism, Vorticism, Rayonism and related early avant-garde
styles.note: Mostly abstract; suits religious or legendary subjects

styles.name: Jacoba van Heemskerck
styles.features: Abstracted trees, ships and landscapes in bold dark-outlined curves and angular planes, glowing reds, blues and greens, compositions resembling stained glass with heavy black leading
styles.section: Cubism, Futurism, Orphism, Vorticism, Rayonism and related early avant-garde

styles.name: Gösta Adrian-Nilsson (GAN)
styles.features: Sharp-angled crystalline sailors, men and machines in dynamic diagonals, saturated reds, blues and blacks, Cubo-Futurist fragmentation, later cool flat geometric abstraction
styles.section: Cubism, Futurism, Orphism, Vorticism, Rayonism and related early avant-garde

styles.name: Marthe Donas
styles.medium: oil and collage on canvas and board
styles.features: Cubist still lifes and female figures with pasted textured materials, sharply cut planes in soft greys, rose and ochre, spare refined geometry, fabric and sand collage elements
styles.section: Cubism, Futurism, Orphism, Vorticism, Rayonism and related early avant-garde

styles.name: Vasily Surikov
styles.features: Large crowded historical canvases, frosty bluish whites and deep crimsons, densely packed figures in old Russian costume, snow and wooden architecture, individually characterised faces, shallow compressed space filled edge to edge.

styles.name: Vasily Perov
styles.features: Sober realist genre painting in muted brown and grey tonality, poor townsfolk, clergy and peasants in everyday scenes, narrative gestures, dim winter light, carefully drawn faces with social detail.

styles.name: Vasily Polenov
styles.features: Fresh sunny realism, light-filled Moscow courtyards and riverbanks, clean greens and whites, crisp cast shadows, small quiet everyday figures, clear air and gentle atmospheric perspective.

styles.name: Alexandre Benois
styles.features: Retrospective scenes of 18th-century palaces and formal gardens, delicate pen line, small promenading courtiers in wigs, pale greens, soft greys and gold, theatrical stage-like perspective with clipped hedges and fountains.

styles.name: Konstantin Somov
styles.features: Nostalgic rococo pastiche, ladies in crinolines and harlequins in twilight parks, fireworks and rainbows, fine precise drawing, porcelain-like faces, pastel pinks, mint greens and dusky blues.

styles.name: Léon Bakst
styles.medium: watercolour, gouache and pencil on paper
styles.features: Theatrical costume designs, dancers in exaggerated twisting poses, flowing patterned fabrics, exotic oriental ornament and jewellery, saturated emerald, orange, violet and gold against blank paper, swift pencil contours.

styles.name: Mstislav Dobuzhinsky
styles.medium: ink, watercolour and gouache on paper
styles.features: Graphic cityscapes with firm ink line and flat washes, blank firewalls, courtyards, fences and gas lamps, muted greys, ochres and dull greens, melancholy empty streets with tiny figures, sharp geometric perspective.

styles.name: Anna Ostroumova-Lebedeva
styles.features: Colour woodcuts of St Petersburg, flat interlocking planes of colour with bold cut contours, canals, bridges, embankments and palace facades, restrained slate blue, black, ochre and pale grey, wide airy skies.

styles.name: Zinaida Serebriakova
styles.features: Luminous figures with smooth rounded volumes, warm golden skin tones, peasant women at harvest, bathhouse and dressing-table scenes, clear contours, soft daylight, earthy ochres and fresh whites.

styles.name: Boris Kustodiev
styles.features: Bright decorative scenes of provincial merchant life, Shrovetide fairs, troikas and onion domes under snow, rosy plump women at tea, saturated reds, blues and whites, high viewpoint, many tiny lively figures.

styles.name: Andrei Ryabushkin
styles.features: Decorative scenes of 17th-century Muscovy, figures in long patterned kaftans and kokoshniks, flat bright costume colours against snow or wooden churches, simplified faces, stiff hieratic poses, gentle humour.

styles.name: Nikolai Fechin
styles.medium: oil on canvas, brush and palette knife
