styles.section: Natural history, botanical, scientific and anatomical illustration from the 16th to 20th c.
styles.note: Lettered labels are integral to the look.

styles.name: Max Brödel
styles.features: Carbon dust rubbed onto textured board, soft tonal gradations from silvery grey to black; surgical views of organs with glistening highlights, hands and instruments in frame, crisp edges where needed, photographic yet simplified.
styles.section: Natural history, botanical, scientific and anatomical illustration from the 16th to 20th c.
styles.note: Medical subject; avoid gore.

styles.name: Ferdinand Bauer
styles.features: Exacting botanical watercolour of a whole plant on a white ground; razor-sharp edges, precisely matched colours, magnified dissections of flower parts and seeds placed around it, flat even lighting, every hair and vein drawn.
styles.section: Natural history, botanical, scientific and anatomical illustration from the 16th to 20th c.

styles.name: Georg Dionysius Ehret
styles.features: An elegant single flowering branch curving across the page, with enlarged dissections of stamens, pistils and seeds in a row below; fine engraved contours, clear transparent colour, white ground, graceful balanced composition.
styles.section: Natural history, botanical, scientific and anatomical illustration from the 16th to 20th c.

styles.name: Basilius Besler florilegium engraving
styles.features: Large folio copper engravings of plants filling the page frontally, with bulbs and roots shown and flowers spread symmetrically; crisp contour and cross-hatching, optional bright hand colouring, monumental flat presentation without background.
styles.section: Natural history, botanical, scientific and anatomical illustration from the 16th to 20th c.

styles.name: Renaissance herbal woodcut, Leonhart Fuchs
styles.features: Whole plants showing roots, flowers and fruit at once, drawn in clean even woodcut outline with almost no shading; flat bright hand-applied colour, stylised symmetrical leaves, plain white page.
styles.section: Natural history, botanical, scientific and anatomical illustration from the 16th to 20th c.

styles.name: Conrad Gessner zoological woodcut
styles.features: Black-and-white woodcuts of animals in profile on a bare ground line; bold outlines and simple parallel hatching, some fanciful armour-like details, naive proportions, each creature isolated like an encyclopedia entry.
styles.section: Natural history, botanical, scientific and anatomical illustration from the 16th to 20th c.

styles.name: Robert Hooke microscopic engraving
styles.features: Copper engravings of insects and tiny objects hugely magnified to fill the sheet; dense cross-hatching and stipple modelling, armour-like plates, bristles and compound eyes, grey monochrome, no background, sculptural light from one side.
styles.section: Natural history, botanical, scientific and anatomical illustration from the 16th to 20th c.

styles.name: Mark Catesby
styles.features: Birds, fish or snakes paired with native plants on one sheet; flat, slightly stiff poses, bold etched outlines, broad hand-applied colour, decorative overlapping shapes, scale ignored, no horizon.
styles.section: Natural history, botanical, scientific and anatomical illustration from the 16th to 20th c.

styles.name: Edward Lear parrot lithographs
styles.features: Life-size parrots perched on simple branches, rendered with soft lithographic crayon texture; fluffed feathers and alert eyes, brilliant hand-coloured greens, reds and blues, pale untouched background, lively individual character.
styles.section: Natural history, botanical, scientific and anatomical illustration from the 16th to 20th c.
styles.note: Specify the bird plates, not his nonsense cartoons.

styles.name: Elizabeth Gould
styles.features: Pairs of birds on branches among flowering plants; hand-coloured lithograph with soft crayon grain, delicate feather texture, gentle naturalistic poses, clear jewel colours, paper left white around the group.
styles.section: Natural history, botanical, scientific and anatomical illustration from the 16th to 20th c.

styles.name: Marianne North
styles.features: Plants painted in their native settings, with flowers or fruit in the foreground and rainforest, mountains or temples behind; dense saturated colour, thick confident strokes, crowded tropical abundance, panoramic depth.
styles.section: Natural history, botanical, scientific and anatomical illustration from the 16th to 20th c.

styles.name: Walter Hood Fitch
styles.features: Hand-coloured lithographs of single plants; flowing confident line, flowers often seen at an angle with leaves cropped at the margin, small floral dissections, fresh clear colour, white page, economical drawing.
styles.section: Natural history, botanical, scientific and anatomical illustration from the 16th to 20th c.

styles.name: Sarah Stone
styles.features: Watercolour and gouache of museum specimens such as exotic birds, shells and curios, shown as rigid mounted figures on a minimal ground; bright opaque colour, careful feather patterns, slightly naive stiffness.
styles.section: Natural history, botanical, scientific and anatomical illustration from the 16th to 20th c.

styles.name: Margaret Mee
styles.features: Gouache of plants and epiphytes in the foreground with misty rainforest, river or trees behind; crisp leaf veins, luminous whites, deep greens, botanical accuracy merged with an atmospheric landscape.
styles.section: Natural history, botanical, scientific and anatomical illustration from the 16th to 20th c.

styles.name: Beatrix Potter mycological watercolours
styles.features: Precise watercolour studies of mushrooms and lichens, showing caps, gills, sections and spores; soft transparent washes, earthy browns, ochres and reds, moss and leaf litter at the base, white paper.
styles.section: Natural history, botanical, scientific and anatomical illustration from the 16th to 20th c.
styles.note: Her name may pull toward picture-book animals; stress the scientific fungus studies.

styles.name: Company school natural history painting, Calcutta
styles.features: Large birds or animals shown life-size on a branch or ground line against bare white paper; fine Mughal-trained brushwork, individually drawn feathers, soft European shading, muted naturalistic colours with bright accents, calm profile poses.
styles.section: Natural history, botanical, scientific and anatomical illustration from the 16th to 20th c.

styles.name: Kawahara Keiga
styles.features: Japanese brush and watercolour adapted to Western specimen drawing: fish, crabs and plants laid out flat on white paper; careful shading, sharp scales, muted natural colours, ink outlines with soft gradations.
styles.section: Natural history, botanical, scientific and anatomical illustration from the 16th to 20th c.

styles.name: Japanese honzōgaku plant illustration, Iwasaki Kan'en
styles.medium: woodblock print with hand colouring on paper
styles.features: Woodblock outlines with hand colouring; plants shown whole from roots to blossoms, slender brushlike lines, soft flat colour, small brushed characters naming species, airy page with visible paper texture.
styles.section: Natural history, botanical, scientific and anatomical illustration from the 16th to 20th c.

styles.name: Canton export natural history painting
styles.medium: watercolour and gouache on Western paper
styles.features: Bright opaque watercolour by Chinese painters working for European collectors: fish, birds, flowers and fruit isolated on white; precise outlines, vivid saturated reds and greens, flattened frontal view, decorative crispness.
styles.section: Natural history, botanical, scientific and anatomical illustration from the 16th to 20th c.

styles.name: Royal Botanical Expedition of New Granada, Mutis school
styles.features: Full-size plants painted in intense mineral greens and reds; smooth flat surfaces, symmetrical leaves, sharp edges, floral dissections drawn in black or sepia ink below, bold and slightly stylised elegance.
styles.section: Natural history, botanical, scientific and anatomical illustration from the 16th to 20th c.

styles.name: von Wright brothers
styles.features: Birds in calm natural poses within Nordic settings of birch, pine, lakeshore and snow; hand-coloured lithograph or oil, careful feather detail, cool clear northern light, muted greys, browns and greens.
styles.section: Natural history, botanical, scientific and anatomical illustration from the 16th to 20th c.

styles.name: Swedish botanical engraving, Johan Wilhelm Palmstruch
styles.features: Small-format hand-coloured copper engravings: one native plant per page with roots, flowers and tiny dissection details; fine outline, clear fresh colour, compact upright composition, white ground.
styles.section: Natural history, botanical, scientific and anatomical illustration from the 16th to 20th c.

styles.name: Flora Danica engraving
styles.features: Hand-coloured copperplate engravings of Nordic plants, mosses, lichens and fungi at life size; delicate outline and hatching, soft natural greens and browns, upright specimen on a white page, sober exactness.
styles.section: Natural history, botanical, scientific and anatomical illustration from the 16th to 20th c.

styles.name: Vasily Vatagin
styles.medium: pencil, charcoal and watercolour on paper
styles.features: Lively animal studies in pencil, charcoal and watercolour: wolves, bears, elephants and monkeys caught mid-movement; quick confident contour, a sense of anatomical weight, sparse wash backgrounds, sometimes carved-wood simplicity.
styles.section: Natural history, botanical, scientific and anatomical illustration from the 16th to 20th c.

styles.name: Jacques de Sève
styles.features: Engravings of animals standing in theatrical settings of classical ruins, balustrades and park landscapes; fine hatching, elegant portrait-like posing, soft grey tones, carefully drawn fur, decorative architecture framing the animal.
styles.section: Natural history, botanical, scientific and anatomical illustration from the 16th to 20th c.

styles.name: Albertus Seba cabinet-of-curiosities engraving
styles.features: Engraved plates densely packed with snakes coiled around birds, lizards, shells and starfish in symmetrical patterns; fine hatching, bright hand colouring, ornamental cabinet-style display, no setting.
styles.section: Natural history, botanical, scientific and anatomical illustration from the 16th to 20th c.

styles.name: Leopold and Rudolf Blaschka
styles.features: Lampworked glass models of jellyfish, sea anemones, octopus and flowers; translucent and opaque glass with painted surfaces, fine filament tentacles, lifelike colour, displayed against a dark museum background, glossy fragility.
styles.section: Natural history, botanical, scientific and anatomical illustration from the 16th to 20th c.

styles.name: Clemente Susini
styles.features: Coloured wax anatomical models: reclining figures and body parts opened to show organs; glossy realistic flesh, red muscle and blue vessels, real hair, silk cushions, glass cases, soft museum lighting.
styles.section: Natural history, botanical, scientific and anatomical illustration from the 16th to 20th c.
styles.note: Anatomical nudity and open bodies; keep it museum-like, not graphic.

styles.name: Nicolas-Henri Jacob
styles.features: Large hand-coloured lithographs of dissected bodies and organs; soft crayon modelling, rich crimsons, pale yellow fat and blue veins, calm ordered layouts, faces and limbs rendered with portrait-like realism.
styles.section: Natural history, botanical, scientific and anatomical illustration from the 16th to 20th c.
styles.note: Graphic anatomy; keep the treatment restrained.

styles.name: Leonardo da Vinci anatomical drawings
styles.medium: pen and ink over red or black chalk on paper
styles.features: Brown ink pen lines over chalk, with cross-hatching that follows the form; layered muscles, bones and organs seen from several angles on one sheet, dense mirror-script notes around the drawings, aged paper.
styles.section: Natural history, botanical, scientific and anatomical illustration from the 16th to 20th c.
styles.note: Mirror-script annotations surround the drawings; any lettering should read as faint handwriting.

styles.name: Santiago Ramón y Cajal
styles.medium: India ink and pencil on paper
styles.features: Black India ink on cream paper: branching neurons, axons and dendrites drawn as fine lines and dots; sparse layering, small letters marking cells, intricate tree-like networks, no colour.
styles.section: Natural history, botanical, scientific and anatomical illustration from the 16th to 20th c.

styles.name: Adolphe Millot encyclopedic plates
styles.features: Encyclopedic colour plates with dozens of insects, birds, mushrooms or shells arranged in neat rows on a pale ground; small numbers beneath, flat bright chromolithographic colour, clear outlines, decorative grid.
styles.section: Natural history, botanical, scientific and anatomical illustration from the 16th to 20th c.
styles.note: Avoid legible captions; small numbers are enough.

styles.name: German school botanical and zoological wall chart
styles.features: Large classroom posters of enlarged plants, insects or animals with cross-sections; bold outlines, flat saturated chromolithographic colour, dark or neutral background, strong legible shapes, frontal diagrammatic layout.
styles.section: Natural history, botanical, scientific and anatomical illustration from the 16th to 20th c.
styles.note: Avoid printed labels to prevent garbled text.

styles.name: Archibald Thorburn
styles.features: Game birds such as grouse, partridge and pheasant in heather moors, snow or woodland; fluid watercolour with gouache highlights, soft feather texture, misty hills, muted purples, browns and greens.
styles.section: Natural history, botanical, scientific and anatomical illustration from the 16th to 20th c.

styles.name: Louis Agassiz Fuertes
styles.features: Birds in crisp watercolour and gouache, in alert natural poses on branches or ground; vivid accurate plumage, sharp eyes, minimal sketched habitat, white paper, fresh field-study energy.
styles.section: Natural history, botanical, scientific and anatomical illustration from the 16th to 20th c.

styles.name: Charles R. Knight
styles.features: Oil paintings of dinosaurs and Ice Age mammals in reconstructed landscapes; soft naturalistic light, swampy or plains settings, earthy greens and browns, animals in mid-action, muscular believable anatomy.
styles.section: Natural history, botanical, scientific and anatomical illustration from the 16th to 20th c.

styles.name: Zdeněk Burian
styles.features: Dense oil reconstructions of prehistoric life: dinosaurs, mammoths and early humans in primeval forests, swamps and tundra; dramatic skies, dark rich greens and browns, moody light, painterly realism.
styles.section: Natural history, botanical, scientific and anatomical illustration from the 16th to 20th c.

styles.name: Elizabeth Blackwell
styles.features: Simple copper engravings of herbs and medicinal plants, one per page; clear outline, flat bright hand colouring, flowers, leaves and sometimes roots, modest naive design, plain white ground.
styles.section: Natural history, botanical, scientific and anatomical illustration from the 16th to 20th c.

styles.name: Joris Hoefnagel
styles.features: Insects, snails and flowers scattered across a vellum page with trompe-l'oeil cast shadows; minute detail, gold oval frames, delicate bright colours, playful arrangement.
styles.section: Natural history, botanical, scientific and anatomical illustration from the 16th to 20th c.

styles.name: Nature printing (Naturselbstdruck)
styles.medium: print from a specimen impressed into lead, electrotype
styles.features: Ferns, seaweeds and leaves printed directly from the specimen's own relief; exact veins and fronds, slight embossed texture, soft natural-coloured inks, flat silhouette, no drawing marks, white paper.
styles.section: Natural history, botanical, scientific and anatomical illustration from the 16th to 20th c.

styles.name: Karl Blossfeldt
styles.features: Black-and-white photographs of magnified buds, seed heads and stems on a plain grey background; frontal symmetry, sculptural forms like wrought ironwork, sharp focus, even lighting, quiet austere presentation.
styles.section: Natural history, botanical, scientific and anatomical illustration from the 16th to 20th c.

styles.name: Étienne Léopold Trouvelot
styles.features: Pastel and chromolithograph images of planets, sunspots, nebulae, comets and aurora; deep black skies, glowing soft gradients, flame-like solar prominences, careful observational detail, cool blues and fiery oranges.
styles.section: Natural history, botanical, scientific and anatomical illustration from the 16th to 20th c.

styles.name: USDA pomological watercolour
styles.features: Watercolour portraits of apples, pears, peaches and citrus: the whole fruit with leaves beside a cut half showing flesh and seeds; precise blushes and russeting, soft shadows, plain white paper.
styles.section: Natural history, botanical, scientific and anatomical illustration from the 16th to 20th c.

styles.name: Émile-Allain Séguy
styles.features: Stencil-coloured pochoir plates of butterflies, beetles and other insects in symmetrical rows or decorative patterns; flat jewel colours, metallic gold and silver, crisp edges, Art Deco ornamental rhythm.
styles.section: Natural history, botanical, scientific and anatomical illustration from the 16th to 20th c.

styles.name: Mary Delany
styles.features: Flowers built from cut and layered coloured paper on a deep black ground; tiny pieces form petals and leaves, flat shapes with slight relief, exact botanical forms, glowing colours, single stem centred.
styles.section: Natural history, botanical, scientific and anatomical illustration from the 16th to 20th c.

styles.name: Beaux-Arts architectural rendering, École des Beaux-Arts, Paris
styles.medium: ink and watercolour wash on stretched paper
styles.features: Precise ink-ruled elevations and sections built up in many transparent graded washes; soft cast shadows at 45 degrees; pale sky gradients; symmetrical classical facades, colonnades and domes; sepia, grey and warm stone tones.
styles.section: Architectural drawing, cartography and technical illustration as imagery

styles.name: Hugh Ferriss
styles.medium: charcoal and carbon pencil on board
styles.features: Smoky charcoal masses of stepped setback skyscrapers rising from fog; dramatic up-lighting and searchlight beams; soft rubbed gradients with little fine detail; monolithic volumes; near-monochrome black, grey and white night atmosphere.
styles.section: Architectural drawing, cartography and technical illustration as imagery

styles.name: Axonometric architectural drawing, De Stijl
styles.features: House volumes shown in parallel axonometric projection from above or below, no converging perspective; flat interlocking planes in primary red, yellow and blue with black, grey and white; crisp ruled edges; planes hovering slightly apart.
styles.section: Architectural drawing, cartography and technical illustration as imagery

styles.name: Architectural blueprint, cyanotype
styles.features: Fine white lines on a deep Prussian-blue ground; orthographic plans, sections and elevations; dimension lines with arrowheads, hatched wall sections, centre lines; slightly mottled blue, faded edges, fold creases and pinholes.
styles.section: Architectural drawing, cartography and technical illustration as imagery
styles.note: Keep annotations as small illegible marks.

styles.name: Leslie Ashwell Wood
styles.medium: gouache, ink and airbrush on board
styles.features: Large machines such as ocean liners, locomotives and airliners with hull or skin peeled away; inner decks, engines and tiny passengers visible; clean ink outlines, flat bright gouache, crisp shading; numbered callouts around the cutaway.
styles.section: Architectural drawing, cartography and technical illustration as imagery

styles.name: Airbrush technical cutaway, mid-20th-century aviation and automotive illustration
styles.medium: airbrush and technical pen on illustration board
styles.features: Three-quarter view of an aircraft or car with skin cut back along jagged edges; every rib, pipe and cylinder in fine ink line; smooth airbrushed metallic gradients; key parts picked out in red or yellow; white background.
styles.section: Architectural drawing, cartography and technical illustration as imagery

styles.name: Exploded-view assembly drawing
styles.features: Mechanical parts separated along straight dashed axis lines, floating apart in isometric projection without perspective; uniform thin black outlines; light parallel hatching for shade; each component aligned to show how it fits into the next.
styles.section: Architectural drawing, cartography and technical illustration as imagery

styles.name: Isometric pixel art of 1990s computer games
styles.features: Buildings and terrain on a diamond grid at a 2:1 isometric angle; hard square pixels without anti-aliasing; limited saturated palette with dithered shading; tiny figures a few pixels tall; rooms shown with front walls removed.
styles.section: Architectural drawing, cartography and technical illustration as imagery

styles.name: Bird's-eye city views of the Civitates Orbis Terrarum (Braun and Hogenberg)
styles.features: Walled town seen from a high oblique angle with every roof, gate and church tower drawn; rivers, fields and roads around; costumed couples standing in the foreground; delicate engraved line washed in soft green, rose and ochre.
styles.section: Architectural drawing, cartography and technical illustration as imagery
styles.note: Leave cartouches and banners blank.

styles.name: Jacopo de' Barbari
styles.features: Immense aerial panorama of a lagoon city from an impossible height; thousands of buildings, canals and moored ships cut in fine black line; rhythmic wavy strokes for water; puffing wind heads in clouds; black on cream paper.
styles.section: Architectural drawing, cartography and technical illustration as imagery

styles.name: Matthäus Merian the Elder
styles.features: Topographic views of towns and castles seen from a nearby hill; crisp orderly engraved lines; layered roofs, spires and fortifications; river foreground with boats; neat hatching for shadow; tiny travellers on roads; black on white.
styles.section: Architectural drawing, cartography and technical illustration as imagery

styles.name: Olaus Magnus, Carta Marina
styles.features: Northern seas swarming with whiskered sea serpents and whales attacking ships; land filled with tiny scenes of skiers, reindeer, castles and battles; swirling hatched waves; woodcut outlines with flat pale colour washes.
styles.section: Architectural drawing, cartography and technical illustration as imagery
styles.note: Render without place names.

styles.name: Dutch Golden Age cartography, Blaeu workshop
styles.features: Coastlines edged with bands of watercolour green, pink and yellow; ornate scrolling cartouches with allegorical figures; galleons and spouting sea monsters on finely hatched seas; compass roses; tiny relief hills; borders with city vignettes.
styles.section: Architectural drawing, cartography and technical illustration as imagery
styles.note: Omit place names; keep cartouches blank.

styles.name: Majorcan cartographic school, Catalan portolan atlas
styles.medium: ink, pigments and gold leaf on vellum
styles.features: Web of radiating rhumb lines over cream parchment; finely fringed coastlines; enthroned kings in tents, camel caravans, red-and-gold domed cities and flags; seas with blue wave patterns; gilded islands and compass rose.
styles.section: Architectural drawing, cartography and technical illustration as imagery
styles.note: Render coastal place names as unreadable hairlines or omit.

styles.name: Kuwagata Keisai
styles.medium: ink and light colour on paper; woodblock print
styles.features: Sweeping aerial panorama of a city seen from above the bay; countless tiny roofs in soft grey-blue; a snowy peak and hills curving along the horizon; light ink lines and pale washes; bay dotted with sails; gently bent land.
styles.section: Architectural drawing, cartography and technical illustration as imagery

styles.name: Chinese jiehua (ruled-line boundary painting)
styles.features: Palaces and pavilions drawn with ruler-straight fine lines in oblique parallel projection, no vanishing point; dense bracket sets, railings and roof tiles; blue-green mountains and drifting clouds; tiny courtiers on terraces; mineral green, azurite and ochre.
styles.section: Architectural drawing, cartography and technical illustration as imagery

styles.name: Joseon pictorial maps (hoehwasik jido)
styles.features: Mountains as continuous green ridgelines branching like veins; rivers as blue bands; county towns as small walled enclosures with tiled roofs; top-down and frontal views combined; bright mineral greens, blues and reds on pale paper.
styles.section: Architectural drawing, cartography and technical illustration as imagery
styles.note: Omit place-name labels.

styles.name: Semyon Remezov
styles.features: Hand-drawn chorographic maps where winding rivers fill the sheet as thick bands; tiny wooden forts, chapels, yurts and camps; trees and hills as little symbols; pale watercolour in green, ochre and blue; no consistent scale.
styles.section: Architectural drawing, cartography and technical illustration as imagery
styles.note: Omit handwritten annotations.

styles.name: Mikhail Makhaev
styles.features: Wide classical perspective views along river embankments; palaces with long regular facades in rigid ruled perspective; broad water with sailing boats and barges; promenading figures and carriages; even engraved lines; high clear sky.
styles.section: Architectural drawing, cartography and technical illustration as imagery

styles.name: Iakov Chernikhov
styles.medium: gouache, ink and pencil on paper
styles.features: Fantastical industrial architecture of cantilevered beams, cylinders and girders in dramatic axonometric or low perspective; vivid flat red, black, blue and yellow; sharp hard shadows; machine-like compositions on plain grounds.
styles.section: Architectural drawing, cartography and technical illustration as imagery

styles.name: Ivan Leonidov
styles.medium: white paint and ink on black board
styles.features: Thin white lines and pale volumes on a matt black ground; slender towers, glass spheres and cable stays; extremely sparse planar layouts on endless flat terrain; whites, greys and a touch of colour.
styles.section: Architectural drawing, cartography and technical illustration as imagery

styles.name: Étienne-Louis Boullée
styles.features: Gigantic pure geometric monuments such as spheres, cones and pyramids in grey and brown wash; vast smooth walls and endless colonnades; theatrical light with deep cast shadows; minute figures emphasising scale; dark cloudy skies.
styles.section: Architectural drawing, cartography and technical illustration as imagery

styles.name: Karl Friedrich Schinkel
styles.medium: pen, ink and watercolour; outline engraving
styles.features: Crisp neoclassical facades and interiors in clean contour line with minimal shading; precise perspective views with a few elegant figures; stage-like vaults in deep starry blue; calm temple fronts against open sky.
styles.section: Architectural drawing, cartography and technical illustration as imagery

styles.name: Joseph Michael Gandy
styles.features: Bird's-eye cutaway of a vast classical building with roofs removed and rooms exposed like ruins; warm golden light in sepia and amber washes; deep shadows in vaults; dense columns, domes and stairs; sometimes fiery skies.
styles.section: Architectural drawing, cartography and technical illustration as imagery

styles.name: Erich Mendelsohn
styles.medium: ink or pencil sketch on paper
styles.features: Small expressive sketches of streamlined buildings in a few sweeping curved strokes; horizontal speed lines and rounded corners; heavy dark ink masses against white; dynamic perspective; gestural, almost no detail.
styles.section: Architectural drawing, cartography and technical illustration as imagery

styles.name: Gordon Cullen
styles.medium: pen and ink with flat tint
styles.features: Lively eye-level townscape sketches of lanes, steps and small squares; confident uneven pen line; flat grey or single-colour tint; bollards, railings, lamps and small strolling people; views unfolding as a walking sequence.
styles.section: Architectural drawing, cartography and technical illustration as imagery

styles.name: Paul Rudolph
styles.features: Sectional perspectives in dense black ink, thousands of fine parallel lines building shadow and texture; ribbed concrete walls and interlocking split levels; sky and voids left white; tiny figures and plants.
styles.section: Architectural drawing, cartography and technical illustration as imagery

styles.name: Helmut Jacoby
styles.medium: technical pen, airbrush and mechanical tone
styles.features: Cool, precise perspective renderings of modernist buildings; razor-fine technical pen lines; smooth grey airbrushed skies and glass reflections; trees as stippled clusters; small elegant figures; mostly black and grey.
styles.section: Architectural drawing, cartography and technical illustration as imagery

styles.name: Eugène Viollet-le-Duc
styles.features: Cutaway and exploded views of Gothic cathedrals, castles and timber roofs; clean ink line with fine hatching; individual masonry blocks, vault ribs and joints; bird's-eye reconstructions of medieval towns; black on white.
styles.section: Architectural drawing, cartography and technical illustration as imagery

styles.name: Encyclopédie technical plates (Diderot and d'Alembert)
styles.features: Top vignette of a workshop with craftsmen at work in a shallow box-like room; below, tools and machine parts laid out flat in orderly rows; clean engraved lines with light even hatching; black on white.
styles.section: Architectural drawing, cartography and technical illustration as imagery
styles.note: Reference letters optional; no captions.

styles.name: Agostino Ramelli
styles.features: Elaborate machines such as water-raising wheels, cranes and rotating reading desks shown in open cutaway, gears, chains and pistons visible through broken walls; tiny operators; landscape backgrounds; firm engraved crosshatching.
styles.section: Architectural drawing, cartography and technical illustration as imagery

styles.name: De re metallica woodcuts (Agricola)
styles.features: Hillsides cut open to reveal shafts, tunnels and ladders; miners with picks, buckets and windlasses; pumps and bellows shown with casings removed; bold black outlines, parallel hatching, naive flattened perspective; uncoloured paper.
styles.section: Architectural drawing, cartography and technical illustration as imagery

styles.name: Patent drawing
styles.features: Strict black-ink line drawings of devices in orthographic and perspective views; uniform line weight; ruled shading lines on one side of forms; numbered leader lines to parts; generous white space; no colour.
styles.section: Architectural drawing, cartography and technical illustration as imagery

styles.name: 19th-century engineering presentation drawing
styles.medium: ink and watercolour wash on paper or tracing linen
styles.features: Orthographic sections of engines, bridges and locomotives in fine ruled ink; conventional material washes: brick red, steel blue, brass yellow, timber umber, iron grey; soft graded shading on cylinders; cream paper with clean margins.
styles.section: Architectural drawing, cartography and technical illustration as imagery

styles.name: Yamato-e fukinuki yatai (blown-off roof view)
styles.medium: ink and mineral colour on paper handscroll
styles.features: Palace interiors seen from a steep overhead diagonal with roofs and ceilings removed; parallel oblique architecture; courtiers in layered robes with line-and-hook faces; flat mineral colours; gold clouds dividing scenes.
styles.section: Architectural drawing, cartography and technical illustration as imagery

styles.name: Heinrich C. Berann
styles.features: Painted panoramic relief maps of mountain ranges and ocean floors seen from a high oblique angle with a bent horizon; crisp snowy peaks, blue-shadowed valleys, detailed rock faces; luminous sky; naturalistic greens and blues.
styles.section: Architectural drawing, cartography and technical illustration as imagery

styles.name: Erwin Raisz
styles.features: Physiographic landform maps: mountains as countless tiny pen strokes and ridge symbols, plateaus stippled, dunes dotted, glaciers outlined; pictorial relief seen obliquely on a flat map; black ink on white.
styles.section: Architectural drawing, cartography and technical illustration as imagery
styles.note: Omit labels.

styles.name: Eduard Imhof
styles.medium: gouache and airbrush relief shading on paper
styles.features: Mountain terrain modelled with soft shaded relief lit from the upper left; high peaks bright and warm, valleys cooler bluish-grey; delicate contours and rock hachures; muted green and yellow lowlands.
styles.section: Architectural drawing, cartography and technical illustration as imagery

styles.name: Relaciones Geográficas pictorial maps of New Spain
styles.features: Flat pictorial maps mixing Indigenous glyphs and European signs; hills as bell-shaped green glyphs; roads marked with rows of black footprints; rivers as blue bands with wavy lines; churches in simple elevation; open paper background.
styles.section: Architectural drawing, cartography and technical illustration as imagery
styles.note: Omit written glosses.

styles.name: Baroque military fortification plan
styles.features: Star-shaped bastioned fortresses in plan with sharp angled ramparts tinted rose and yellow; moats in pale blue-green; zigzag siege trenches; tiny tents and gun batteries; green fields, ruled ink outlines, compass rose.
styles.section: Architectural drawing, cartography and technical illustration as imagery

styles.name: Gothic architectural drawing on parchment
styles.medium: ink on parchment, compass and straightedge
styles.features: Tall cathedral facade and spire elevations in thin brown ink, every line ruled or compass-drawn; tracery, pinnacles and gables repeated in strict symmetry; faint scored construction lines; no shading; yellowed parchment.
styles.section: Architectural drawing, cartography and technical illustration as imagery

styles.name: Villard de Honnecourt
styles.features: Sketchbook leaves mixing cathedral details, machines, animals and draped figures; brown ink outline with sparse hatching; geometric construction triangles and grids inside faces and bodies; flat, diagrammatic Gothic drawing.
styles.section: Architectural drawing, cartography and technical illustration as imagery

styles.name: Andrea Palladio, treatise woodcut plates
styles.features: Symmetrical villa plans, half elevations and sections side by side; clear black outlines on white with minimal hatching for openings; columns, pediments, porticoes and domes in strict proportion; no landscape or figures.
styles.section: Architectural drawing, cartography and technical illustration as imagery

styles.name: Marion Mahony Griffin
styles.medium: ink and watercolour on linen or silk
styles.features: Tall or long panoramic compositions with low horizontal houses half-hidden behind foreground branches and foliage, layered like Japanese prints; fine ink line; flat muted greens, golds and browns.
styles.section: Architectural drawing, cartography and technical illustration as imagery

styles.name: Lebbeus Woods
styles.medium: graphite, coloured pencil and ink on paper
styles.features: Scarred, war-torn cities grafted with jagged metallic shells and spiked scaffolds; obsessively hatched graphite; sharp fragments and curved plates; dramatic perspective; mostly grey with rust and blue accents.
styles.section: Architectural drawing, cartography and technical illustration as imagery

styles.name: Aldo Rossi
styles.medium: felt pen, watercolour and oil on paper
styles.features: Metaphysical cities of archetypal shapes such as cones, cubes, cabins, tall chimneys and coffee pots crowded together; flat sky blue, brick red and yellow; naive outlines; long shadows over empty piazzas.
styles.section: Architectural drawing, cartography and technical illustration as imagery

styles.name: Bruno Taut
styles.features: Visionary crystalline glass buildings crowning mountain peaks; faceted prisms, star shapes and arches with radiating light lines; pale iridescent blue, pink and green watercolour; sparse ink outlines; Alpine landscape.
styles.section: Architectural drawing, cartography and technical illustration as imagery

styles.name: Erik Dahlbergh
styles.features: Bird's-eye views of palaces, manors and towns with geometric parterre gardens; regular engraved perspective; finely hatched cloudy skies; small carriages, riders and strollers; lakes and rocky northern hills.
styles.section: Architectural drawing, cartography and technical illustration as imagery

styles.name: Soviet popular-science magazine illustration
styles.features: Futuristic machines, space stations and atomic cities as bright cutaways and perspective panoramas; flat saturated gouache in blue, orange and red; smooth sky gradients; small optimistic workers; bold simplified technical detail.
styles.section: Architectural drawing, cartography and technical illustration as imagery

styles.name: Andreas Cellarius
styles.features: Celestial charts with concentric planetary orbits around sun or earth; zodiac and constellation figures; corners filled with astronomers, instruments and cherubs on clouds; rich hand colour in blue, gold, rose and green; ornate borders.
styles.section: Architectural drawing, cartography and technical illustration as imagery
styles.note: Omit labels.

styles.name: Ferdinando Galli-Bibiena
styles.medium: pen, ink and brown wash on paper
styles.features: Stage-set palaces and arcades in angled two-point perspective; endless receding colonnades, coffered vaults and staircases; brown ink line with fluid wash shading; theatrical diagonal views; few small figures.
styles.section: Architectural drawing, cartography and technical illustration as imagery

styles.name: Hans Vredeman de Vries
styles.features: Perspective studies of tiled floors, arcades, courtyards and colonnades receding to a single vanishing point; strict orthogonal lines; checkered pavements; small figures and Renaissance ornament; clean parallel hatching.
styles.section: Architectural drawing, cartography and technical illustration as imagery

styles.name: Wenzel Jamnitzer
styles.features: Ornamental geometric solids such as faceted polyhedra, star bodies, hollow lattice frames and rings floating above plain pedestals; precise linear perspective; even hatching on facets; black on white; crystalline effect.
styles.section: Architectural drawing, cartography and technical illustration as imagery

styles.name: Daguerreotype
styles.features: Mirror-like silver plate with a shimmering positive-negative sheen, extremely fine detail, stiff frontal sitters from long exposures, soft oval vignette, blue and amber tarnish halo around the edges, brass mat frame in a velvet case.
styles.section: Historic photography processes and deceased photographers
styles.note: Monochrome only; sitters rarely smile.

styles.name: Calotype salted paper print
styles.medium: salted paper print from paper negative
styles.features: Matte warm-brown image sunk into the paper fibres, soft grainy detail from the paper negative, broad masses of light and shadow, mottled texture, faded reddish-brown to lilac tones, static buildings and posed groups.
styles.section: Historic photography processes and deceased photographers

styles.name: Albumen print
styles.medium: albumen silver print from glass negative, card-mounted
styles.features: Thin glossy paper with warm sepia to purple-brown tones, crisp detail, yellowed faded highlights, fine surface crazing, pale blank skies, mounted on cream card with gilt edges or rounded corners.
styles.section: Historic photography processes and deceased photographers

styles.name: Ambrotype
styles.medium: collodion negative on glass backed with black varnish
styles.features: Thin collodion image on glass that reads as a positive against black backing, creamy grey highlights, deep blacks, shallow focus, cheeks sometimes tinted pink by hand, set behind a brass mat in a hinged case.
styles.section: Historic photography processes and deceased photographers

styles.name: Tintype
styles.features: Dark grey-brown image on a black-lacquered metal plate, low contrast with milky highlights, shallow depth with blurred edges, stiff frontal poses, scratches, flaking emulsion, swirling pour marks and darkened corners.
styles.section: Historic photography processes and deceased photographers

styles.name: Cyanotype
styles.medium: iron-salt sun print on watercolour paper
styles.features: Prussian-blue ground with white and pale blue tones, sun-printed on rag paper, visible brushed edges of the coating, soft detail, flat contact-printed plants or translucent layered silhouettes resembling a blueprint.
styles.section: Historic photography processes and deceased photographers
styles.note: Monochrome blue only.

styles.name: Platinum print
styles.medium: platinum or palladium print on matte paper
styles.features: Matte velvety surface with a very long smooth grey scale, cool silver-grey to warm brown-black tones, delicate glowing highlights, soft deep shadows, no gloss, image embedded in the paper fibres.
styles.section: Historic photography processes and deceased photographers

styles.name: Gum bichromate print
styles.medium: pigmented gum arabic print on drawing paper
styles.features: Painterly pigment print on textured paper, visible brushed coating, coarse granular tones in sepia, terracotta or green-grey, soft blurred detail, highlights dissolving into bare paper, halfway between photograph and charcoal drawing.
styles.section: Historic photography processes and deceased photographers

styles.name: Bromoil print
styles.medium: oil ink brushed onto bleached gelatin silver print
styles.features: Oil ink dabbed by brush onto the print, stippled grainy texture, simplified tonal masses, soft haloed edges, ink-black to warm brown tones, misty landscapes, harbours and street scenes with detail lost in atmosphere.
styles.section: Historic photography processes and deceased photographers

styles.name: Pictorialism, Photo-Secession
styles.medium: platinum, gum and gelatin silver prints
styles.features: Soft-focus monochrome images imitating painting and etching, misty diffused backlight, muted sepia, grey or green toning, tonal harmony over detail, contemplative figures, twilight cityscapes, wooded landscapes, textured art papers.
styles.section: Historic photography processes and deceased photographers

styles.name: Autochrome Lumière
styles.medium: colour glass transparency with dyed starch grains
styles.features: Colour built from dyed potato-starch grains giving a visible pointillist speckle, soft muted pastel greens, rose and violet, low contrast, dark grainy shadows, slight blur on moving parts, sunlit gardens and posed figures.
styles.section: Historic photography processes and deceased photographers
styles.note: Subjects held still; no snapshot action.

styles.name: Sergey Prokudin-Gorsky three-colour photography
styles.features: Rich saturated yet natural colour from three separate exposures, sharp detail, red-green-blue fringes on moving water, leaves and figures, posed villagers and workers, onion domes, wooden churches, monasteries, rivers and railways.
styles.section: Historic photography processes and deceased photographers

styles.name: Photochrom
styles.features: Flat soft colours laid over a crisp monochrome photographic base, chalky turquoise seas, pinkish skies, ochre buildings, slightly unreal uniform tints, travel views of towns, harbours, markets and mountains.
styles.section: Historic photography processes and deceased photographers

styles.name: Yokohama hand-coloured albumen photography
styles.features: Albumen prints delicately tinted by hand, soft pink faces, blue and red kimono, green foliage, studio-posed figures with parasols and props before painted backdrops, temple gates, bridges and landscape views.
styles.section: Historic photography processes and deceased photographers

styles.name: Stereoview card
styles.medium: paired albumen prints on curved card mount
styles.features: Two near-identical sepia images side by side with arched tops on a buff card, deep receding perspective, foreground objects placed to enhance depth, travel scenes, monuments, street views and interiors.
styles.section: Historic photography processes and deceased photographers

styles.name: Carte de visite studio portrait
styles.medium: small albumen print on stiff card
styles.features: Small full-length sepia studio portrait, sitter posed beside balustrade, column or swag drape, painted backdrop, braced stiff posture, even north light, ornamental printed studio imprint below the image.
styles.section: Historic photography processes and deceased photographers

styles.name: Kodachrome slide colour photography, mid-century
styles.features: Saturated deep reds, yellows and blues, dense rich shadows, fine grain, slightly warm cast, crisp detail, bright daylight scenes of cars, diners, holiday travel and street life, framed like a projected slide.
styles.section: Historic photography processes and deceased photographers

styles.name: Dye-transfer colour print
styles.features: Deep, dense, pigment-like colour saturation, velvety blacks, precise controlled hues, glossy surface, strong reds and greens, studio still lifes, advertising products and colour landscapes with rich shadow detail.
styles.section: Historic photography processes and deceased photographers

styles.name: Integral instant film photograph, 1970s
styles.features: Small square image in a thick white frame with a wider bottom margin, soft dreamy focus, shifted colours with cyan shadows and creamy warm highlights, low contrast, chemical blotches at edges, intimate domestic snapshots.
styles.section: Historic photography processes and deceased photographers

styles.name: Man Ray
styles.medium: gelatin silver print, photogram and solarisation
styles.features: Cameraless photograms with glowing white silhouettes of everyday objects on black, solarised portraits with dark outline halos around faces, sleek surreal still lifes, high-contrast silver tones.
styles.section: Historic photography processes and deceased photographers

styles.name: Julia Margaret Cameron
styles.medium: albumen print from wet collodion negative
styles.features: Soft-focus close-up portraits, faces emerging from deep shadow, loose hair and draped costume, intentional blur, scratches and fingerprints on the plate, warm brown tones, allegorical and literary tableaux.
styles.section: Historic photography processes and deceased photographers

styles.name: Nadar
styles.features: Half-length portraits against a plain neutral backdrop, sitters in dark clothing, strong side light from a studio window modelling the face, frank direct expressions, rich brown tones, almost no props.
styles.section: Historic photography processes and deceased photographers

styles.name: Carleton Watkins
styles.features: Very large prints with vast sharp detail, granite cliffs, waterfalls and giant trees, high blank white skies, mirror-still river reflections, clean classical compositions, warm brown tones.
styles.section: Historic photography processes and deceased photographers

styles.name: Timothy O'Sullivan
styles.medium: albumen print from wet collodion glass negative
styles.features: Barren desert canyons and eroded rock formations, tiny figures or survey wagons for scale, bleached white skies, stark geology, warm albumen tones, austere empty distances.
styles.section: Historic photography processes and deceased photographers

styles.name: Eadweard Muybridge
styles.features: Grids of consecutive frames showing a horse, athlete or animal in motion against a gridded backdrop, crisp silhouettes, phases of movement side by side in rows, neutral grey-brown tones.
styles.section: Historic photography processes and deceased photographers
styles.note: A sequence grid, not a single scene.

styles.name: Vittorio Sella
styles.medium: large glass-plate negative, gelatin silver print
styles.features: High-mountain panoramas with razor-sharp ice ridges, crevasses and seracs, tiny roped climbers, deep gradation from black rock to luminous snow, darkened skies, crisp clear alpine air.
styles.section: Historic photography processes and deceased photographers

styles.name: Eugène Atget
styles.medium: gold-toned albumen print from glass negative
styles.features: Quiet empty Paris streets, courtyards, shopfronts and park statues at dawn, warm brown-violet tones, lens vignetting in the corners, ghostly blurred passers-by from long exposures, reflections in shop windows.
styles.section: Historic photography processes and deceased photographers

styles.name: Gertrude Käsebier
styles.features: Soft-focus portraits of mothers and children, warm brown tones, simple dim interiors with window light, figures in white dresses, gentle intimate gestures, painterly diffused edges.
styles.section: Historic photography processes and deceased photographers

styles.name: Edward Weston
styles.medium: gelatin silver contact print from 8x10 negative
styles.features: Sharp close-up still lifes of peppers, shells and cabbages, sculptural curves in soft light against black, smooth silver tones, extreme detail, also rippled sand dunes and gnarled cypress trees.
styles.section: Historic photography processes and deceased photographers

styles.name: Ansel Adams
styles.features: Black-and-white mountain landscapes with deep black skies, brilliant white clouds and snow, full tonal range from pure black to white, razor-sharp granite, rivers and trees, dramatic storm light.
styles.section: Historic photography processes and deceased photographers

styles.name: Imogen Cunningham
styles.features: Close-up black-and-white plant forms such as magnolias, calla lilies and succulents, sharp sculptural petals and leaves on dark grounds, smooth gradations, abstracted geometry, also direct intimate portraits.
styles.section: Historic photography processes and deceased photographers

styles.name: Bernd and Hilla Becher
styles.medium: gelatin silver prints arranged in grids
styles.features: Grids of frontal black-and-white photographs of water towers, blast furnaces, winding towers and gas tanks, flat overcast light, centred subjects, white skies, identical viewpoint and scale, no people.
styles.section: Historic photography processes and deceased photographers

styles.name: Maxim Dmitriev
styles.medium: albumen and gelatin silver print from glass negative
styles.features: Wide views of Volga river towns, fairs, ferries, barges and landing stages, peasants and pilgrims as many small figures, wooden churches, sharp detail, warm brown tones, broad river horizons.
styles.section: Historic photography processes and deceased photographers

styles.name: I. K. Inha
styles.medium: gelatin silver print from glass negative
styles.features: Black-and-white views of Karelian villages, log houses, rune singers in traditional dress, lakes and spruce forests, soft northern light, still water reflections, quiet grey tones and unhurried rural scenes.
styles.section: Historic photography processes and deceased photographers

styles.name: Lewis Hine
styles.features: Documentary black and white of child workers in mills, mines and streets, children posed facing the camera among machinery, rows of spindles, window light and flash, smudged faces, gritty tonal realism, ironworkers high on steel girders.
styles.section: Historic photography processes and deceased photographers

styles.name: Margaret Bourke-White
styles.features: Monumental black-and-white industrial images of steel mills with pouring molten metal, dams, turbines and repeating gears, dramatic lighting, low angles, bold geometric patterns, glowing sparks in darkness.
styles.section: Historic photography processes and deceased photographers

styles.name: Weegee
styles.medium: gelatin silver print, press camera with flash
styles.features: Harsh on-camera flash at night, blown-out white faces against pitch-black backgrounds, crime scenes, fires and gawking crowds, rain-slicked streets, raw snapshot framing, grainy high-contrast tabloid black and white.
styles.section: Historic photography processes and deceased photographers

styles.name: Brassaï
styles.medium: gelatin silver print, long night exposure
styles.features: Paris at night: wet cobblestones, lamp halos in fog, bridges, cafés and dance halls, deep velvety blacks, glowing pools of gaslight, grainy silver tones, couples and night-time figures.
styles.section: Historic photography processes and deceased photographers

styles.name: Henri Cartier-Bresson
styles.features: Black-and-white street scenes caught at a precise instant, figures mid-leap or mid-stride, strong geometric composition with lines and shapes aligned, natural light, no flash, full mid-grey tonal range.
styles.section: Historic photography processes and deceased photographers

styles.name: Robert Doisneau
styles.features: Humanist black-and-white street photographs of Paris, children playing, couples, cafés, bistros and bakers, gentle humour, soft grey daylight, candid ordinary people, cobbled streets and shop windows.
styles.section: Historic photography processes and deceased photographers

styles.name: Josef Sudek
styles.medium: gelatin silver and pigment print, panoramic camera
styles.features: Soft melancholy black-and-white Prague: misty panoramas of rooftops and the river, condensation-fogged studio windows, still lifes of glass and fruit, dense quiet shadows, warm grey tones.
styles.section: Historic photography processes and deceased photographers

styles.name: Vivian Maier
styles.medium: square-format gelatin silver print, twin-lens reflex camera
styles.features: Square black-and-white street portraits from a waist-level camera, strangers caught close, children and elderly people, reflections and shadow self-portraits, Chicago and New York sidewalks, crisp medium-format detail.
styles.section: Historic photography processes and deceased photographers

styles.name: Saul Leiter
styles.medium: colour slide film and gelatin silver
styles.features: Colour street views through rain-streaked or steamy windows, large blurred dark foreground shapes, small vivid red umbrellas or yellow cabs in muted fields, snow, layered reflections, painterly near-abstraction.
styles.section: Historic photography processes and deceased photographers

styles.name: Fred Herzog
styles.features: Colour street views of Vancouver, neon signs, finned cars, barbershops and pawnshops, saturated warm reds and teals, working people on sidewalks, layered storefronts, sunlit detail, mid-century urban ordinariness.
styles.section: Historic photography processes and deceased photographers

styles.name: Ernst Haas
styles.features: Colour photographs with deliberate motion blur, swirling streaks of saturated colour, bullfights, dancers and birds dissolving into movement, reflections in puddles, rich reds and golds, abstract textures of weathered walls.
styles.section: Historic photography processes and deceased photographers

styles.name: Fan Ho
styles.medium: gelatin silver print, twin-lens reflex camera
styles.features: Black-and-white Hong Kong streets in shafts of hard sunlight and smoke, small lone figures in deep geometric shadow, steep alleys and staircases, high-contrast silver gradation, hazy luminous air.
styles.section: Historic photography processes and deceased photographers

styles.name: Mario Giacomelli
styles.features: Extreme high-contrast black and white with harsh grain, near-graphic blacks and whites, patterned ploughed hillsides seen from above, dark-robed young priests playing in snow that dissolves into pure white.
styles.section: Historic photography processes and deceased photographers

styles.name: Malick Sidibé
styles.features: Candid black-and-white party and dance snapshots of young people in Bamako, flash-lit dancers in flared trousers, couples twisting, records held up, studio portraits with striped backdrops and chequered floors.
styles.section: Historic photography processes and deceased photographers

styles.name: Lala Deen Dayal
styles.medium: albumen and gelatin silver print from glass negative
styles.features: Wide sharp views of Indian palaces, temples, forts and stepwells, carefully arranged groups of courtiers, officials and hunting parties, ornate carved detail, warm sepia tones, pale skies.
styles.section: Historic photography processes and deceased photographers

styles.name: Frank Hurley
styles.medium: glass-plate gelatin silver print and early colour plates
styles.features: Polar expedition photographs: ship locked in pack ice, frost-coated rigging, sledging teams and dogs, endless icy wastes, flash-lit night scenes, dramatic composite skies, cold grey tones.
styles.section: Historic photography processes and deceased photographers

styles.name: Harold Edgerton
styles.medium: high-speed stroboscopic gelatin silver and colour print
styles.features: Strobe-frozen motion: milk-drop crowns, bullets bursting through apples, multiple-exposure sequences of athletes and swinging golf clubs, crisp edges and bright highlights on black backgrounds.
styles.section: Historic photography processes and deceased photographers

styles.name: Max Penson
styles.features: Black-and-white scenes of Soviet Uzbekistan: cotton harvests, new canals and tractors, people in striped robes and embroidered skullcaps, dynamic angles, bright Central Asian sunlight, crisp contrast.
styles.section: Historic photography processes and deceased photographers

styles.name: J. M. W. Turner, late watercolours
styles.medium: watercolour on white paper, washes, scraping and lifting
styles.features: Luminous transparent washes of gold, rose and pale blue that dissolve solid forms into light and mist. Wet blooms, scratched-out highlights, buildings and boats reduced to faint smudges, vast skies taking most of the sheet.

styles.name: John Sell Cotman, Norwich School watercolour
styles.features: Flat interlocking planes of clear wash with crisp edges, almost like cut paper. Simplified trees, bridges and rocks, still water with reflections, cool greens, ochres and grey-blues, very little linear detail.

styles.name: Paul Sandby, topographical tinted drawing
styles.medium: pen and ink with watercolour and bodycolour on paper
styles.features: Neat pen outlines tinted with light washes, clear daylight, accurate views of castles, country houses and town streets. Small staffage figures, carts and horses, pale blue skies, tidy foreground trees framing the scene.

styles.name: Peter De Wint
styles.features: Long horizontal sweeps of rich wash, flat fenland and harvest fields, low horizons, wide grey skies. Deep greens, browns and golden stubble, cattle and haywains as dark blots, loose wet edges.

styles.name: Francis Towne
styles.medium: pen and ink outline with watercolour washes
styles.features: Firm pen contours enclosing flat pale washes, mountains and rocks simplified into clear geometric planes. Restrained greens, blue-greys and buff, strong pattern, almost no atmospheric blur.

styles.name: John Ruskin, nature and architecture studies
styles.medium: pencil, pen, watercolour and bodycolour on paper
styles.features: Meticulous close studies of rock strata, lichen, leaves, feathers and Gothic carved capitals. Fine hatching and stippled colour, central area finished while edges fade to bare pencil and blank paper.

styles.name: Helen Allingham
styles.features: Soft detailed watercolour of thatched cottages with rose-covered walls, hollyhocks and foxgloves. Mothers in aprons, small children, hens, warm afternoon light, gentle greens and brick reds, fine stippled texture.

styles.name: John Frederick Lewis
styles.features: Minutely detailed watercolour with opaque highlights, Cairo courtyards and interiors, carved wooden lattice screens casting dappled light. Rich striped textiles, tiled floors, slow figures in robes, warm amber and turquoise.
styles.note: Avoid exoticising stereotypes

styles.name: Edward Lear, topographical landscape watercolours
styles.medium: pencil and pen outline with watercolour washes
styles.features: Quick pen contour over pencil, pale sparing washes of ochre, olive and sky blue. Wide Greek, Albanian and Egyptian landscapes, mountain ridges, small towns, much bare paper left, light travel-sketch feel.
styles.note: Originals often carry small handwritten colour notes; optional

styles.name: John Singer Sargent, watercolours
styles.medium: transparent watercolour with wax resist on white paper
styles.features: Bold fast fluid strokes, white paper left for glare, strong sunlight and deep blue-violet shadows. Venetian canals, gondolas, marble facades, figures lounging in white dresses, forms suggested rather than outlined.

styles.name: Winslow Homer, watercolours
styles.features: Clear saturated washes laid in few strokes, scraped whites for foam and light. Turquoise Caribbean seas, palms, fishermen in boats, Adirondack lakes, leaping trout, strong outdoor daylight.

styles.name: Andrew Wyeth, drybrush watercolour
styles.features: Thin nearly dry brush dragged in fine strokes, tawny dry grass blade by blade, weathered clapboard houses and barns. Muted ochre, brown, grey and white, quiet empty rural spaces, solitary figures.

styles.name: Silverpoint drawing, Renaissance metalpoint
styles.features: Fine even grey lines that tarnish to warm brown, delicate parallel hatching, no erasing, no thick strokes. Paper prepared with pale blue, rose or ivory ground, white heightening, quiet portrait heads and hands.

styles.name: Leonardo da Vinci, red chalk studies
styles.features: Warm red chalk with fine parallel hatching slanting from upper left to lower right, soft smoky modelling. Studies of heads, old men in profile, muscles, horses and plants, several studies scattered on one sheet.

styles.name: Hans Holbein the Younger, chalk portrait drawings
styles.medium: black and coloured chalks with ink accents on pink-primed paper
styles.features: Clean economical contour, faces modelled with soft sparse chalk on pale pink ground, touches of ink for eyes and hat edges. Calm head-and-shoulders portraits, caps, fur collars, minimal background.

styles.name: Rembrandt, pen-and-wash sketches
styles.medium: reed pen and brown ink with brush wash on paper
styles.features: Fast broken reed-pen lines, few strokes for a figure, quick brown wash shadows, lots of bare paper. Biblical scenes, everyday people, flat Dutch fields, farmhouses and windmills sketched with great economy.

styles.name: Claude Lorrain, wash drawings
styles.medium: pen and brown ink with brown wash on paper
styles.features: Broad brown wash in several tones, untouched paper glowing as sunlight, dark silhouetted tree masses, distant hills dissolving in light. Classical ruins, rivers, small shepherds, airy open composition.

styles.name: Antoine Watteau, trois crayons
styles.medium: red, black and white chalk on buff paper
styles.features: Red, black and white chalk combined on warm toned paper, quick flickering strokes. Several studies of heads, hands, women in shimmering silk dresses and musicians scattered across one sheet, graceful turned poses.

styles.name: Jean-Honoré Fragonard, red chalk garden views
styles.features: Lively red chalk in flickering strokes, towering cypresses and umbrella pines, terraced Italian gardens with fountains and balustrades. Tiny strolling figures, bright untouched paper as sunlight, feathery foliage.

styles.name: Edgar Degas, pastels
styles.medium: pastel on paper, layered and fixed
styles.features: Layered pastel hatching in vivid strokes, dancers in tutus, bathers and milliners, off-centre cropped compositions seen from above. Stage footlights, turquoise, orange and rose accents, visible strokes across bodies.

styles.name: Mary Cassatt, pastels
styles.features: Broad zigzag pastel strokes, intimate close views of mothers bathing or holding children. Soft pinks, peach, pale blues and greens, flattened patterned wallpaper and dresses, sketchy unfinished edges.

styles.name: Odilon Redon, noirs
styles.medium: charcoal and black chalk on tinted paper
styles.features: Velvety deep charcoal blacks, glowing pale areas emerging from darkness, dreamlike floating heads, single eyes, strange plants and creatures. Soft smudged gradients, no colour, quiet uncanny mood.

styles.name: Georges Seurat, conté crayon drawings
styles.medium: conté crayon on textured laid paper
styles.features: No outlines, forms built entirely from soft tonal masses of grainy black crayon catching paper texture. Glowing halos where light meets dark, silent silhouetted figures, lamps, trees, riverbanks.

styles.name: Charles Dana Gibson, pen-and-ink illustration
styles.features: Confident sweeping pen line, crisp cross-hatching, tall elegant women with piled-up hair, gentlemen in evening dress. Drawing-rooms, beaches and ballrooms suggested with sparse strokes, clean white space.

styles.name: Léon Bakst, theatre costume designs
styles.medium: watercolour, gouache and pencil with gold paint on paper
styles.features: Single dancing figures in twisting energetic poses on bare paper, elongated limbs, swirling patterned costumes. Saturated orange, emerald, violet and gold, pencil underdrawing visible, ornament and jewellery detail.
styles.note: Original sheets carry handwritten notes; omit lettering

styles.name: Zinaida Serebriakova, pastels
styles.features: Soft directional pastel strokes, sunlit rounded figures, peasant women, children, Moroccan market scenes. Warm ochre, rose, white and blue, calm faces with large dark eyes, light open backgrounds.

styles.name: Egon Schiele, works on paper
styles.medium: gouache, watercolour and pencil on paper
styles.features: Angular wiry contour line, gaunt twisted figures with bony hands, patches of red, orange and ochre gouache on bare paper. Unfinished bodies floating in empty space, sharp nervous energy.
styles.note: Many originals are nudes; keep clothed subjects

styles.name: Paul Klee, watercolours
styles.features: Translucent overlapping squares and rectangles of colour in a loose grid, small childlike signs, arrows, domes and stars. Thin delicate lines, warm ochre, rose, sky blue and green, gentle glowing light.

styles.name: Emil Nolde, watercolours
styles.medium: wet-in-wet watercolour on absorbent Japan paper
styles.features: Saturated colour bleeding into soaked paper, no outlines, soft blooms and edges. Blazing red poppies, sunflowers, stormy seas and flaming skies, deep purples, cadmium yellows and intense blues.

styles.name: Charles Rennie Mackintosh, late landscape watercolours
styles.features: Flattened ordered landscapes, rocks, fields and houses reduced to crisp geometric patterns with firm outlines. Clear Mediterranean light, terracotta, ochre, slate blue and grey-green, almost architectural design.

styles.name: Beatrix Potter, watercolour illustration
styles.medium: watercolour over pen and pencil on paper
styles.features: Small delicate watercolours, accurately drawn rabbits, mice, ducks and hedgehogs, some in simple country clothes. Soft greens and browns, cottage gardens, stone walls, fells, white vignette edges.
styles.note: Use generic animals, not her trademarked characters

styles.name: Hermannsburg School watercolour (Albert Namatjira)
styles.features: Crisp detailed watercolour of ghost gums with white trunks, red-ochre ranges, mauve and blue distant hills. Clear dry light, sharp shadows, detailed foreground spinifex, rock faces and dry creek beds.
styles.note: Secular landscape tradition; do not add Aboriginal sacred symbols

styles.name: Company painting, India
styles.features: Indian artists working for British patrons: fine outlines, soft washes, little shadow, plain empty backgrounds. Carefully observed birds and plants, craftsmen and servants shown in profile with tools, festivals, monuments.

styles.name: Adolph Menzel, drawings and gouaches
styles.medium: carpenter's pencil, graphite and gouache on paper
styles.features: Soft broad graphite smudged with fingers, quick close studies of hands, faces, workers and rumpled interiors. Gouache scenes of crowded ballrooms and factories, glancing light, glittering details, intense observation.

styles.name: Meiji Japanese watercolour (suisaiga)
styles.features: Western-style transparent watercolour of quiet Japanese countryside: thatched farmhouses, rice paddies, temple gates, misty mountains. Soft greys, greens and pale ochres, gentle atmospheric distance, small figures with umbrellas.

styles.name: Victor Hugo, ink wash drawings
styles.medium: brown ink, wash, charcoal and stencils on paper
styles.features: Dark brooding ink blots, stains and splatters shaped into ruined castles, lighthouses and stormy seas. Sepia and black with sudden pale light, textures pressed from lace, dramatic gloomy romantic mood.

styles.name: Minoan fresco, Knossos and Akrotiri
styles.features: Flat unshaded areas of red ochre, blue and yellow on pale plaster; slender wasp-waisted figures in profile with large frontal eye; red-brown men, white-skinned women; lilies, swallows, dolphins, wavy band borders; patchy worn surface.
styles.section: Mural, fresco and public art traditions worldwide

styles.name: Ancient Egyptian tomb painting, Theban New Kingdom
styles.medium: mineral pigments on mud and gypsum plaster
styles.features: Composite figures with profile head, frontal eye and shoulders, striding legs; flat colour fields with crisp dark outlines; horizontal registers on pale ground; ochre skin, Egyptian blue, green; hierarchical scale; neat rows of offerings, papyrus marshes, fish.
styles.section: Mural, fresco and public art traditions worldwide
styles.note: Hieroglyph columns are typical but can be omitted.

styles.name: Roman wall painting, Pompeii and Herculaneum
styles.features: Wall divided into large cinnabar red, black and ochre panels; painted columns, cornices and receding architectural vistas; small framed mythological scenes and floating figures; garlands, candelabra, birds, fruit still lifes; soft impressionistic brushwork with highlights.
styles.section: Mural, fresco and public art traditions worldwide

styles.name: Ajanta cave painting
styles.medium: mineral pigments on clay and lime plaster
styles.features: Crowded continuous narrative without frames; graceful supple figures with heavy-lidded eyes, swaying hips and fine jewellery; warm ochres, malachite green, lapis blue; soft modelling along contours; palaces, elephants, forests flowing into each other.
styles.section: Mural, fresco and public art traditions worldwide
styles.note: Narratives are Buddhist Jataka tales; keep to courtly and everyday scenes.

styles.name: Sigiriya rock painting
styles.medium: pigments on lime plaster over rock face
styles.features: Half-length female figures emerging from stylised clouds; full rounded bodies, almond eyes, elaborate tiaras and jewellery, hands holding flowers; warm yellow, orange and red-ochre skin, green accents; fluid confident outlines on pale plaster.
styles.section: Mural, fresco and public art traditions worldwide
styles.note: Figures are traditionally bare-chested; clothe them for general audiences.

styles.name: Tang dynasty tomb murals, Qianling
styles.medium: ink and colour on whitewashed plaster
styles.features: Loosely spaced groups of court ladies and attendants on plain pale ground; flowing even ink contours, light washes of red, green and ochre; high topknot hairstyles, long high-waisted skirts, shawls; carried fans, cups and boxes.
styles.section: Mural, fresco and public art traditions worldwide

styles.name: Goguryeo tomb murals
styles.medium: pigments on plastered or stone tomb walls
styles.features: Horsemen with bows chasing tigers and deer across stylised wavy mountain bands; rows of dancers in polka-dot robes; flat figures with simple ink outlines; red, black and ochre on light ground; floating lotus and cloud motifs.
styles.section: Mural, fresco and public art traditions worldwide

styles.name: Sogdian wall painting, Afrasiyab, Samarkand
styles.features: Processions of envoys and riders on horses, camels and a white elephant; figures in richly patterned silk robes with roundel motifs; deep blue ground, earth reds and whites; flat profile figures with strong outlines; boats among fish and water birds.
styles.section: Mural, fresco and public art traditions worldwide

styles.name: Catalan Romanesque fresco, Pyrenean valley churches
styles.features: Frontal hieratic figures with almond eyes and thick black contours; drapery reduced to geometric parallel folds; backgrounds of horizontal colour bands in ochre, blue, red and white; flat, no depth; strong symmetry and beaded borders.
styles.section: Mural, fresco and public art traditions worldwide
styles.note: Mostly Christian iconography; works for legends and allegorical figures.

styles.name: Dionisius (Dionisy), Muscovite fresco painter
styles.features: Elongated weightless figures with small heads and gently swaying poses; light luminous palette of sky azure, pale ochre, soft pink, cherry and white; delicate rhythmic contours; symmetrical calm groups; thin slab-like hills and pale architecture.
styles.section: Mural, fresco and public art traditions worldwide
styles.note: Church iconography; adapt to legends and processions.

styles.name: Painted monasteries of Bukovina, Moldavian exterior fresco
styles.features: Entire outer church walls covered with horizontal registers of figures under wide shingled eaves; intense blue or ochre-red grounds; rows of saints and crowded narrative scenes of sieges and judgment; linear Byzantine figures; weathered surface.
styles.section: Mural, fresco and public art traditions worldwide

styles.name: Renaissance sgraffito facade decoration, Bohemia
styles.features: Two-tone facades: dark grey or black plaster scratched away to reveal white beneath; illusionistic diamond-point rustication blocks; friezes of figures, hunts, battles and allegories in crisp line; graphic engraving-like hatching across whole walls.
styles.section: Mural, fresco and public art traditions worldwide

styles.name: Lüftlmalerei, Alpine facade painting
styles.features: Whitewashed house fronts painted with trompe-l'œil window surrounds, pilasters and balconies; scenes of saints, hunters, peasants and fairy tales between windows; clear bright colours, blue skies, rococo scrolls; overhanging wooden eaves.
styles.section: Mural, fresco and public art traditions worldwide

styles.name: Hälsingland farmhouse decoration
styles.medium: distemper on wooden walls and linen
styles.features: Painted farmhouse rooms: large flowing flower-and-foliage scrolls in red, blue, green and ochre; marbled panels and borders; naive biblical and local figures in 18th-century dress; flat colour, loose confident brushwork, every surface decorated.
styles.section: Mural, fresco and public art traditions worldwide

styles.name: Ethiopian church painting, Gondarine style
styles.medium: tempera on cloth fixed to walls and ceilings
styles.features: Flat bright figures with large almond eyes and round frontal faces; strong black outlines; saturated red, yellow, green and blue; stacked registers; horsemen, battles and saints; ceilings tiled with rows of winged faces.
styles.section: Mural, fresco and public art traditions worldwide
styles.note: Mostly church imagery; secular battle and royal scenes fit best.

styles.name: Mughal wall painting, Fatehpur Sikri and Agra
styles.medium: pigment and gold on polished lime plaster
styles.features: Shallow painted niches holding flower vases, cypresses or flowering plants; delicate arabesque scrolls and gold detailing; soft red, green, blue and ivory on burnished plaster; occasional small landscapes and figures in Persianate manner.
styles.section: Mural, fresco and public art traditions worldwide

styles.name: Mughal tile mosaic, Lahore Fort Picture Wall
styles.medium: cut glazed tile mosaic set in brick
styles.features: Long red-brick wall inset with framed glazed tile panels; elephant fights, polo players, horsemen, cranes, winged figures and dragons; turquoise, cobalt, yellow, green and white tile pieces; flat silhouettes within geometric borders.
styles.section: Mural, fresco and public art traditions worldwide

styles.name: Shekhawati haveli wall painting
styles.features: Merchant mansion walls covered inside and out with framed panels; flat figures in profile; Krishna stories, elephants, horses and camels beside trains, cars and Europeans; ochre, indigo, red, green; dense rows of painted arches and borders.
styles.section: Mural, fresco and public art traditions worldwide

styles.name: Tibetan historical palace murals, Lhasa
styles.features: Bird's-eye narrative panoramas of builders, caravans, processions, horsemen and tents; turquoise and malachite-green rounded hills, lapis skies, curling cloud scrolls; fine outlines with gold highlights; many small figures without single-point perspective.
styles.section: Mural, fresco and public art traditions worldwide
styles.note: Avoid deities and protector figures; keep to historical, building and daily-life scenes.

styles.name: Safavid palace wall painting, Isfahan
styles.features: Courtly banquets with musicians, dancers and wine servers; slender figures with oval faces, small mouths and patterned silk robes; flat stylised trees and flowers; gold accents, warm reds and blues; large wall panels and small garden-lovers niches.
styles.section: Mural, fresco and public art traditions worldwide

styles.name: Kano school sliding-door painting, Momoyama period
styles.medium: ink and mineral colour on gold leaf, paper sliding doors
styles.features: Massive pine and cypress trunks in bold ink sweeping across gold-leaf grounds; tigers, hawks, cranes; malachite green and azurite blue; golden cloud bands cutting the scene; one continuous composition running across several panels.
styles.section: Mural, fresco and public art traditions worldwide

styles.name: Thai temple mural painting, Rattanakosin period
styles.medium: tempera and gold leaf on plaster
styles.features: Continuous epic scenes separated by zigzag lines; graceful flat figures in dance-like poses; gilded crowns and tiered palace roofs; masked demon warriors; dark green or red grounds; dense small scenes of village life.
styles.section: Mural, fresco and public art traditions worldwide
styles.note: Temple setting; epic battles and village life are the best subjects.

styles.name: Portuguese azulejo tile panel
styles.features: Blue on white painted tile panels covering walls; visible square tile grid; scenes of hunts, ships, gardens and city views in brushy cobalt washes; ornate baroque frames of scrolls, putti and acanthus; glossy surface.
styles.section: Mural, fresco and public art traditions worldwide

styles.name: Talavera poblana tile cladding, Puebla
styles.medium: tin-glazed earthenware tiles set in red brick
